# Cipi

> Cipi is a free, open-source (MIT) platform that turns a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 VPS into a hardened hosting server for Laravel and PHP apps, with zero-downtime Git deploys, an optional self-hosted web panel, a REST API and MCP servers for AI assistants. A self-hosted alternative to Laravel Forge, Ploi and Vito Deploy: no subscription, nothing leaves your server.

Install: `wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash` (as root on a fresh server). Then log in as `cipi` and run `sudo cipi …`.

## Key facts

- **Free and self-hosted.** MIT licence. No account, no SaaS control plane, no telemetry. The only cost is the VPS.
- **Isolated apps.** Each app gets its own Linux user, PHP-FPM pool (`open_basedir`), database user, Nginx vhost, certificate and deploy key.
- **App types.** Laravel (PHP-FPM or Octane with FrankenPHP), Node apps (SPA, static, SSR with Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix, Vite), and custom PHP apps (WordPress, Symfony, static sites).
- **Zero-downtime deploys.** Deployer releases with one atomic symlink swap, `cipi deploy <app> --rollback`, pre-deploy DB snapshots, health-checked automatic rollback, a hash-chained deploy audit trail. Push-to-deploy from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps (automatic setup with a token) or any Git server.
- **cipi.yml.** An app's server settings in its repository: PHP version and ini, aliases, www/apex, workers, Horizon, Reverb, scheduler, Meilisearch, health check, deploy options and post-deploy steps, extra databases, crons, backup profiles, redirects, proxies, Node settings. `cipi yml plan` shows every change; `apply` is all-or-nothing; `auto on` applies after every deploy. `cipi-<env>.yml` per environment (the server chooses the file). Fail-closed: namespaced resources, allowlisted runners, no secrets.
- **Runtime.** Several PHP versions side by side (8.3–8.6; new servers default to 8.6), MariaDB (default) and optional PostgreSQL, one Valkey instance per app, optional Meilisearch, Node runtimes, Supervisor workers, Horizon, Reverb behind the app's own domain, Octane with pinned FrankenPHP builds, per-app JIT.
- **Security.** SSH keys only, UFW, fail2ban (configurable attempts), optional CrowdSec, Cloudflare Zero Trust (tunnel, Access, close ports), encrypted vault (AES-256) for credentials, nightly PHP patching from packages.sury.org at 03:30 with alerts while a version is vulnerable, nginx from nginx.org mainline with `cipi autoupdate`, HTTP/2 never enabled, hardened PHP-FPM admin flags, malware scans, compliance reports.
- **Operations.** Backup profiles to local and S3-compatible destinations (encrypted, retention, verification), `cipi sync` to move or replicate apps between servers, server monitor, health checks, disk usage per app and database, notifications by e-mail, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Mattermost, Google Chat, ntfy, Pushover or webhook.
- **Interfaces.** CLI first. Optional web panel (`cipi gui <domain>`): fleet view of many servers, roles and per-app permissions, invite links, TOTP 2FA, OpenID Connect SSO. REST API (`cipi api <domain>`) with Sanctum tokens and abilities, IP allowlist, Swagger. cipi-cli (Go binary for your laptop), PHP SDK (`cipi/sdk`), WHMCS module.
- **AI.** Two MCP servers: the Cipi Agent's per-app MCP (`composer require cipi/agent`, `/cipi/mcp`: health, logs, DB schema and capped queries, Artisan, deploy, cipi.yml validation; SQL and Artisan guards, secret redaction) and the server MCP of the API (`/mcp`). Plus a GDPR-safe database anonymizer.
- **Requirements.** Full VM or bare metal (KVM, VMware, Hyper-V, Xen HVM), Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, public IPv4, ports 22, 80, 443. Not for local Docker, WSL or LXC.

## Site

English only, unprefixed URLs. Docs: https://cipi.sh/docs/ — Guides: https://cipi.sh/guides/ (RSS: https://cipi.sh/guides/feed.xml) — Comparisons: https://cipi.sh/alternatives — cipi.yml: https://cipi.sh/cipi-yml — Source: https://github.com/cipi-sh — News: https://t.me/cipicloud

Full plain-text content: https://cipi.sh/llms-full.txt

# Documentation


## Quickstart

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/quickstart

From a fresh Ubuntu server to a Laravel app on HTTPS, in about fifteen minutes. Every step shows the real command and what it prints; click a terminal to jump to the end.

```flow
Install | one command on the server
Log in | as cipi, with your SSH key
Create an app | isolated user, DB, PHP
Deploy | zero downtime from Git
HTTPS | Let's Encrypt, auto-renewed
```

**You need:** an Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 VPS with a public IP, a domain whose DNS you control, and a Git repository. Cipi is free; the only cost is the server.

## 1. Install Cipi 

SSH into the fresh server as root (or a sudo user) and run the installer. It asks for your SSH public key, shows its plan, then installs and hardens the whole stack.

Save the credentials it prints. Requirements, SSH keys and unattended installs: [Install Cipi](https://cipi.sh/docs/installation).

## 2. Log in as cipi 

Root login over SSH is now off. Connect as `cipi` with your key and prefix commands with `sudo` (no password needed for `cipi`).

## 3. Create your first app 

The wizard asks for the app type, runtime, database, name, domain and repository, then builds an isolated app: its own Linux user, database, PHP pool, Nginx vhost, worker and deploy key.

Skip the questions with flags:

```bash
$ sudo cipi app create --user=myapp --domain=myapp.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/myapp.git --branch=main
```

> [!warning] The summary at the end (database password, deploy key, webhook token, a `mariadb+ssh://` URL for TablePlus or DBeaver) is shown **once**. Save it.

## 4. Connect the repository 

If you gave the installer a Git token, there is nothing to do: Cipi added the deploy key and the push webhook to the repository. Otherwise add the `ssh-ed25519 …` key from the summary as a **read-only deploy key**:

| Provider | Where |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub | Repository → Settings → Deploy keys |
| GitLab | Settings → Repository → Deploy keys |
| Bitbucket | Repository settings → Access keys |
| Azure DevOps | User settings → SSH public keys |

Then check that the server can read it: `sudo cipi git check myapp`. Tokens and automatic setup: [Git providers](https://cipi.sh/docs/git).

## 5. Prepare the Laravel project 

Cipi keeps cache, sessions and queues in each app's **own database**, so no app can read another's data. Laravel 11+ ships those tables; on an older project create them once and commit:

```bash
$ php artisan cache:table && php artisan session:table && php artisan queue:table
```

Migrations run on every deploy. Prefer Valkey for speed or Horizon? Switch per app in [Valkey](https://cipi.sh/docs/valkey).

## 6. Deploy 

The new release is built in its own folder, migrated, then made live with one atomic symlink swap. Visitors never see a half-deployed app, and `cipi deploy myapp --rollback` goes back in a second. How it works: [Deploy & roll back](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploying).

## 7. Turn on HTTPS 

Point the domain's DNS at the server, then:

The certificate covers the domain and its aliases and renews itself. Behind the Cloudflare proxy use `--dns=cloudflare` and set SSL/TLS to **Full (strict)**. More in [SSL certificates](https://cipi.sh/docs/ssl).

## 8. Optional: the web panel 

Prefer a browser, or need one for clients? Install the API and the panel, each on its own domain. The panel can manage this server and any other Cipi server you connect.

## Next steps 

| To… | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy on every `git push` | [Auto-deploy on push](https://cipi.sh/docs/auto-deploy) |
| Run queues or Horizon | [Queues & Horizon](https://cipi.sh/docs/workers) |
| Back up to S3 every night | [Backups to S3](https://cipi.sh/docs/backups) |
| Keep server settings in the repo | [cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml) |
| Get alerts on Slack or Telegram | [Notifications](https://cipi.sh/docs/notifications) |


## Install Cipi

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/installation

One command turns a fresh Ubuntu server into a hardened, production-ready host. This page covers what the server needs, the SSH key, the installer and how you log in afterwards.

## Requirements

| Need | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 LTS**, fresh install | Cipi owns the whole stack; an existing web stack would conflict |
| **Full VM or bare metal** (KVM, VMware, Hyper-V, Xen HVM) | Cipi tunes the firewall, swap and kernel, which needs its own kernel |
| **Public IPv4**, ports 22, 80, 443 open | Let's Encrypt and your visitors must reach the server |
| Root or sudo access | To install packages and harden SSH |

Works on DigitalOcean, Hetzner, AWS EC2, Vultr, Linode, Google Cloud, OVH, Scaleway and any KVM or bare-metal host. The installer checks the environment first: in a container (Docker, LXC, OpenVZ, WSL, OrbStack…) it stops and tells you why.

> [!warning] **Cipi is for real servers, not laptops.** A local VM or container may look like it works, but certificates, domains and deploys will not. See [Why not local?](https://cipi.sh/docs/design-decisions#why-not-local).

## Install

```flow
SSH key | on your laptop
Installer | on the server
Plan & confirm | nothing changes until you say yes
Stack + hardening | ~10 minutes
Credentials | shown once, stored encrypted
```

### 1. Get your SSH public key 

On **your computer** (not the server), print your public key, or create one if you have none:

```bash
$ cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub                       # existing key
$ ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com"     # create one (Enter = default path)
```

Copy the whole `ssh-ed25519 AAAA… comment` line. Only the `.pub` file is public; never paste the private `id_ed25519`.

### 2. Run the installer on the server 

```bash
$ ssh root@your-server-ip
$ wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash
```

On AWS, log in as `ubuntu` and run `sudo -s` first. The installer then:

1. Asks for your public key (and any more: a second laptop, a colleague) before installing anything.
2. Shows its plan: IP, OS, SSH access, stack, passwords. Answer `n` and nothing has changed.
3. Installs Nginx, PHP, MariaDB, Valkey, Supervisor, Composer, Deployer, Certbot, UFW and Fail2ban, and hardens SSH.
4. Prints the credentials (root, MariaDB, Valkey) and waits until you confirm you saved them.
5. Offers the optional extras: a Git provider token (so deploy keys and webhooks are set up for you), the panel API and the web panel.

### Unattended install 

Pass the key in `SSH_PUBKEY` (several keys: one per line). Without a terminal the installer asks nothing.

```bash
$ SSH_PUBKEY="ssh-ed25519 AAAA..." wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash
```

## What the installer secures 

| Area | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| SSH | Root login off; `cipi` user with **key only**; 3 attempts, 20 s grace; X11 off |
| Firewall | UFW allows only 22, 80, 443 |
| Brute force | Fail2ban with progressive bans |
| Patches | Unattended security upgrades |
| Secrets | Root, database and Valkey passwords are random and stored **encrypted** (AES-256) in `/etc/cipi/server.json` |
| Logs | Rotation and retention for app, security and HTTP logs ([Log retention](https://cipi.sh/docs/log-retention)) |

## Log in after the install 

| Who | How |
| --- | --- |
| You (admin) | `ssh cipi@server` with your key, then `sudo cipi …` (no password) |
| Root | From the `cipi` session: `su root` with the root password from the summary |
| An app | `ssh myapp@server` with the app's password, or `su - myapp` as root |

```bash
$ ssh cipi@your-server-ip
$ sudo cipi status          # any cipi command, no password
$ su root                   # full root shell when you need one
```

> [!tip] Lost the credentials? `sudo cipi credentials` prints them again; `sudo cipi credentials export` writes a CSV your password manager can import.


## How Cipi works

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/how-cipi-works

Cipi is a command-line tool that lives on your server. It installs a proven open-source stack, then creates and runs apps on it, each one sealed off from the others. There is no external service in the loop: no account, no agent phoning home, nothing to pay.

## The server

```stack
Nginx | web server, TLS, proxy
PHP-FPM / Octane | several PHP versions side by side
MariaDB / PostgreSQL | one database per app
Valkey | cache, queues (opt-in per app)
Supervisor | workers, Horizon, Reverb
```

| Component | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **Nginx** (nginx.org mainline) | Web server, reverse proxy, TLS termination, HTTP/2 hardening |
| **PHP-FPM** | PHP runtime per app; 8.3 to 8.6 installable side by side |
| **Laravel Octane (FrankenPHP)** | Optional long-running PHP server per Laravel app |
| **MariaDB** | Default database; **PostgreSQL** optional, chosen per app |
| **Valkey** | Open-source Redis fork for cache, sessions, queues, broadcasting |
| **Supervisor** | Keeps queue workers, Octane, Horizon and Reverb running |
| **Deployer** | Atomic, zero-downtime releases (checksum-verified install) |
| **Certbot** | Let's Encrypt certificates and renewals |
| **UFW + Fail2ban** | Firewall and brute-force bans |
| **unattended-upgrades** | Automatic security patches |
| **cipi** | The CLI that ties it all together |

## Each app 

Every app is a separate Linux user. If one app is compromised, the others' files, database and processes are out of reach.

| Area | What the app gets |
| --- | --- |
| Isolation | Its own Linux user (home `750`), PHP pool or Octane process, SSH deploy key |
| Web | An Nginx vhost tuned for Laravel; aliases, redirects, basic auth |
| PHP | Version per app, changeable any time; `php.ini` via [cipi ini](https://cipi.sh/docs/php#cli-ini) |
| Data | Its own database and user (MariaDB or PostgreSQL); its own Valkey instance |
| Processes | Queue workers or Horizon, scheduler, optional Reverb |
| Deploys | Zero-downtime releases, last 5 kept, one-command rollback |
| TLS | Let's Encrypt, HTTP or Cloudflare DNS validation, wildcards |
| Safety nets | Health check after each deploy with automatic rollback, backups, monitoring |

**Laravel** is the default app type. `--node` builds and serves a React, Vue, Next.js, Nuxt or Astro frontend; `--custom` hosts WordPress or plain PHP without database or workers.

## On disk

```tree
/home/myapp/                 # the app's Linux user (chmod 750)
├── .ssh/id_ed25519(.pub)    # deploy key
├── .deployer/deploy.php     # generated Deployer config
├── current -> releases/3/   # the live release (atomic symlink)
├── releases/1 … 5/          # last 5 releases, for rollback
├── shared/
│   ├── .env                 # written by Cipi, kept across releases
│   └── storage/             # persistent storage
└── logs/                    # nginx, php-fpm, worker, deploy logs
```

| Outside the home | Path |
| --- | --- |
| PHP-FPM pool (FPM apps) | `/etc/php//fpm/pool.d/myapp.conf` |
| Nginx vhost | `/etc/nginx/sites-available/myapp` |
| Supervisor programs | `/etc/supervisor/conf.d/myapp.conf` |
| Scheduler | the app user's crontab |
| Database | `myapp` with user `myapp@localhost` |

Cipi writes `.env` with every credential and `APP_KEY`; change it with [cipi app env](https://cipi.sh/docs/environment). If permissions get mangled (an archive unpacked as root, a `chmod 775 .ssh`), `cipi app fix-permissions myapp` restores them. Do not `chown -R`: Nginx writes logs as `www-data` and SSH refuses a deploy key with loose permissions.


## Create an app

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/create-app

One command creates a complete, isolated app: Linux user, PHP pool (or Octane), Nginx vhost, database, worker, scheduler, deploy key and a ready `.env`.

## Pick the app type 

| Type | For | Flag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Laravel** (default) | Laravel apps, on PHP-FPM or Octane | none, or `--octane` |
| **Node** | React, Vue, Svelte, Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix | `--node=spa\|static\|ssr` |
| **Custom** | WordPress, plain PHP, static files, SFTP-only sites | `--custom` |

Details per type: [Laravel Octane](https://cipi.sh/docs/octane), [Node apps](https://cipi.sh/docs/node-apps), [Custom PHP & static sites](https://cipi.sh/docs/custom-apps).

## Interactive 

```bash
$ cipi app create
```

The wizard asks, with the default pre-selected (Enter accepts it): app type, PHP-FPM or Octane, database engine, then name, domain, repository, branch, PHP version and an optional asset build. Before the summary it **tests the deploy key** against the repository; if it cannot read it, it offers to save a Git token and register the key for you.

## With flags 

Any type flag skips the menus; without a terminal every default applies.

```bash
$ cipi app create --user=myapp --domain=myapp.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/myapp.git --branch=main --php=8.6

# Octane, PostgreSQL, front-end build
$ cipi app create --user=api --domain=api.myapp.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/api.git --octane --engine=pgsql \
    --node-build='npm ci && npm run build'

# A staging copy of the same repository
$ cipi app create --user=myapp-stg --domain=staging.myapp.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/myapp.git --branch=develop --env=staging
```

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--user` | Linux user and app name: unique, lowercase, alphanumeric | asked |
| `--domain` | Primary domain; sets the vhost and `APP_URL` | asked |
| `--repository` | Git URL over **SSH** (`git@…`) | asked (required for Laravel) |
| `--branch` | Branch to deploy | `main` |
| `--php` | An installed PHP version (8.3–8.6) | server default |
| `--octane` | Serve with Octane (FrankenPHP) instead of PHP-FPM | off |
| `--engine` | `mariadb` or `pgsql` (after `cipi db install pgsql`) | `mariadb` |
| `--valkey` | `shared` to use the server's Valkey instead of the app's own | own instance |
| `--node-build` | Asset build run in every deploy (npm, npx, yarn, pnpm, bun, node) | none |
| `--env` | Environment label: sets `APP_ENV` and picks `cipi-.yml` | `production` |

## After creation 

The summary shows the server IP for DNS, the deploy key, the database credentials with a `mariadb+ssh://` URL for TablePlus or DBeaver, and the webhook URL and token. **It is shown once.**

```flow
Save the summary | shown once
Deploy key on Git | automatic with a token
Point DNS | A record → server IP
cipi deploy | first release
cipi ssl install | HTTPS
```

> [!tip] With a Git provider token configured, the deploy key and the push webhook are added to the repository automatically. See [Git providers & deploy keys](https://cipi.sh/docs/git).

## In the web panel 

Create an app from the browser: the same wizard, with a server picker. The [web panel](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui) is optional; everything here also works from the CLI.


## Laravel Octane

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/octane

Laravel Octane keeps your app booted in memory and serves requests with FrankenPHP. Typical result: much lower response times for the same hardware. Octane and PHP-FPM apps run side by side on one server.

## Create or convert 

Your repository needs `laravel/octane`, installed with `php artisan octane:install --server=frankenphp`. Octane starts after the first deploy.

```bash
$ cipi app create --user=myapp --domain=myapp.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/myapp.git --octane
$ cipi app convert myapp --to=octane     # an existing FPM app
$ cipi app convert myapp --to=fpm        # and back
$ cipi app limits myapp --octane-workers=4
```

## What Cipi sets up 

```flow
Nginx | static files, proxy to Octane
Octane on 127.0.0.1 | port 8100–8999
FrankenPHP build | pinned per app
Supervisor | keeps it running, reloads on deploy
```

| Piece | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Nginx | `proxy_pass` to the app's local port; static files from `current/public`; no PHP-FPM pool |
| Process | Supervisor program `myapp-octane`, next to the queue workers |
| Deploys | The pinned FrankenPHP binary is linked into each release, then Octane reloads |
| `.env` | `OCTANE_SERVER=frankenphp`, `OCTANE_HTTPS=true` |

Converting rewrites the vhost, process, deploy recipe and `.env`, and keeps the certificate. It turns [JIT](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-jit) off; enable it again if you use it.

## FrankenPHP builds, pinned per app 

The PHP an Octane app runs is the one compiled into its FrankenPHP binary. Cipi keeps those binaries in `/opt/cipi-frankenphp/builds/` (read-only to apps) and **pins one per app**. A deploy never downloads a new binary, so PHP changes only when you decide.

```bash
$ cipi frankenphp                      # each app's build and PHP, patched or not
$ cipi frankenphp upgrade myapp        # newest build on the same PHP minor
$ cipi frankenphp upgrade --all
$ cipi frankenphp use myapp            # pin a specific build
$ cipi frankenphp import ./frankenphp  # a build you compiled (other PHP minor)
$ cipi frankenphp adopt myapp          # pin the binary Octane downloaded
$ cipi frankenphp prune                # remove unused builds
```

| Rule | Why it keeps you stable |
| --- | --- |
| Upgrades stay on the app's PHP minor and FrankenPHP major | No surprise PHP 8.5 → 8.6 jump |
| Octane must answer after an upgrade, or the previous build returns | A bad build never stays live |
| A deploy that needs a newer FrankenPHP stops before migrations | The live release is untouched; run `cipi frankenphp upgrade` |
| Apps on different PHP minors use different builds | 8.5 and 8.6 coexist |
| Nightly patches via `cipi autoupdate` (component `frankenphp`) | Security fixes without manual work |

To move an app to a new PHP minor: `cipi app edit myapp --php=8.6`, then `cipi frankenphp upgrade myapp`.

> [!tip] Octane serves HTTP only. Run long jobs on [queue workers or Horizon](https://cipi.sh/docs/workers) and WebSockets on [Reverb](https://cipi.sh/docs/reverb).


## PHP JIT per app

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/php-jit

PHP's JIT compiles hot code to machine code. It helps CPU-bound work (calculations, big collections, heavy templating) and does little for requests that mostly wait on the database. Cipi turns it on for **one app**, FPM or Octane, and checks it before and after.

```bash
$ cipi app jit myapp on                              # tracing mode, 128M buffer
$ cipi app jit myapp on --mode=function --buffer=256M
$ cipi app jit myapp off
$ cipi app jit myapp --json                          # current state
```

| Check | When | If it fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP can start with JIT (no Xdebug/pcov, JIT compiled in) | Before | Refused, nothing written |
| PHP-FPM active / Octane answering | After | Previous setting restored |

| Runtime | Where the setting goes | Side effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP-FPM | The app's pool, plus a small server-wide file that makes JIT startable for that PHP version | Restarts that version's PHP-FPM (all its apps, briefly) |
| Octane | The app's own ini directory | Restarts only that app's Octane |

A value forced with [cipi ini](https://cipi.sh/docs/php#cli-ini) wins. `cipi app convert` resets JIT. Panel API: `GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/jit`.

> [!tip] Measure before and after on your real workload; keep JIT only where it pays.


## Node apps

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/node-apps

Node apps build and serve modern front-ends with the same lifecycle as Laravel apps: releases, rollback, webhook, SSL, basic auth, redirects, proxies and the deploy audit.

```bash
# Vite SPA: build, serve dist/ with an index.html fallback
$ cipi app create --user=web --domain=web.example.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/web.git --node=spa --framework=vite
# Pre-rendered site (Astro, Nuxt generate, Next export)
$ cipi app create --user=docs --domain=docs.example.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/docs.git --node=static --output=dist
# Node server with blue/green deploys
$ cipi app create --user=shop --domain=shop.example.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/shop.git --node=ssr --framework=next --node-version=24
```

## Modes 

| Mode | Nginx | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spa` | Serves the build; unknown paths fall back to `/index.html` | Client-side routed apps |
| `static` | Serves the build; real 404s via `/404.html` | Pre-rendered sites |
| `ssr` | Proxies to a Node process on localhost, WebSockets included | Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix, Astro SSR |

Hashed assets (`assets/`, `_astro/`, `_nuxt/`, `_app/immutable/`) are cached as immutable; HTML is never cached.

## Options 

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--framework` | Preset: `vite` (spa), `next`, `nuxt`, `sveltekit`, `astro`, `remix` (ssr). Explicit flags win |
| `--node-version` | LTS major: `22` or `24` (default: the [server default](https://cipi.sh/docs/nodejs)) |
| `--build` | Build command (default `npm run build`) |
| `--start` | SSR start command, a Node runner plus arguments, e.g. `node build` |
| `--output` | Build folder for spa/static; the deploy fails if it has no `index.html` |
| `--health-path` | SSR path that must answer below 500 before a release takes traffic (default `/`) |

The build installs from your lockfile (`npm ci`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `yarn install --immutable`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`) with `NODE_ENV=production`. `shared/.env` is read at build time and by SSR servers at runtime; edit it with [cipi app env](https://cipi.sh/docs/environment).

## Zero-downtime SSR: blue/green 

```flow
Start new release | on the idle slot
Health check | must answer  [!security] The switch runs as root through a narrow rule: ports, start command, Node version and health path come from a root-owned file, not from the app. `.env` is read as data, never executed; `HOST` is forced to `127.0.0.1` and the start command runs without a shell.

## Manage 

```bash
$ cipi node status shop                 # mode, commands, slots
$ cipi node restart shop                # zero downtime
$ cipi node logs shop --lines=100
$ cipi app edit shop --start="node .output/server/index.mjs" --health-path=/health
$ cipi app edit web --node=static --output=dist
```

The same settings can live in your repository in the [`node:` section of cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml). Push-to-deploy works without a Laravel agent: Cipi ships a hardened webhook receiver that verifies GitHub/Bitbucket signatures and GitLab/Azure tokens.

> [!note] Node apps get no database by default; add one with [cipi db](https://cipi.sh/docs/databases). `cipi sync` and `cipi app clone` do not handle Node apps yet.


## Custom PHP & static sites

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/custom-apps

Custom apps host anything that isn't Laravel or a Node build: WordPress and other CMSs, plain PHP, static files. Code lives in `~/htdocs`, deployed from Git or uploaded over SFTP.

| | Laravel app | Custom app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deploy | Zero-downtime releases | Pull into `htdocs` |
| Database, `.env` | Created | Add one with `cipi db create` if needed |
| Workers, scheduler | Yes | No |
| Git | Required | Optional (SFTP-only works) |

```bash
# From Git, serving the dist/ folder
$ cipi app create --custom --user=mysite --domain=mysite.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:you/mysite.git --docroot=dist
# SFTP only: no repository
$ cipi app create --custom --user=blog --domain=blog.example.com
$ cipi db create --name=blog              # e.g. for WordPress
```

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Document root | `htdocs/` or a subfolder (`--docroot=public`, `dist`, `www`) |
| Nginx | `index index.html index.php`, `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$args`, `404.html` |
| SFTP-only | Placeholder `index.html`; upload to `~/htdocs` as the app user (SFTP, SCP, rsync) |
| With Git | `cipi deploy mysite` pulls the branch into `htdocs` |

> [!security] Every vhost refuses `/cipi.yml` and `/cipi-*.yml`, so a config file committed to the web root is never served.


## Manage apps

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/manage-apps

Everything you do to an app after creating it: inspect, change, convert, clone, delete. Every change is applied in place, with zero downtime where the runtime allows it.

## Inspect 

| Command | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi app list` | Every app: domain, PHP, status (`suspended` when offline) |
| `cipi app show myapp` | Domain, PHP or Node mode, environment, workers, deploy key, webhook, redirects, proxies |

## Change 

`cipi app edit` flags can be combined in one call.

| Command | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi app edit myapp --php=8.6` | Moves pool, vhost, workers, cron, deploy recipe and `.env` to the new PHP. No downtime |
| `cipi app edit myapp --domain=new.example.com` | New primary domain; the old one becomes an alias; vhost, `APP_URL`, webhook and certificate follow |
| `cipi app edit myapp --branch=develop` | Deploy another branch (also updates `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH`) |
| `cipi app edit myapp --env=staging` | New environment label: `APP_ENV`, `CIPI_ENV`, and reads `cipi-staging.yml` |
| `cipi app edit myapp --repository=git@…` | Attach or change the repository (e.g. turn an SFTP site into a Git one) |
| `cipi app edit myapp --node-build='npm ci && npm run build'` | Front-end build in every deploy; `--no-node-build` removes it |
| `cipi app edit myapp --node-version=24` | Pin Node for this app's builds; `default` follows the server |
| `cipi app edit myapp --predeploy-snapshot` | Dump the database before every deploy ([Safe deploy](https://cipi.sh/docs/safe-deploy)) |
| `cipi app convert myapp --to=octane\|fpm` | Switch runtime ([Laravel Octane](https://cipi.sh/docs/octane)) |
| `cipi app jit myapp on\|off` | PHP JIT for this app ([PHP JIT](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-jit)) |

On an Octane app, changing PHP moves CLI, cron and workers at once; web workers follow when you pin a matching [FrankenPHP build](https://cipi.sh/docs/octane#cli-frankenphp).

## Credentials 

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi app reset-password myapp` | New SSH/SFTP password for the app user, shown once |
| `cipi app reset-db-password myapp` | New database password, written to `.env` in the same step |
| `cipi app webhook recreate myapp --rotate-secret` | Recreate the Git webhook with a new secret |

## Delete 

```bash
$ cipi app delete myapp            # asks for confirmation
$ cipi app delete myapp --force    # for scripts
```

Removes the user, files, database, vhost, PHP pool, workers, search keys and every rule Cipi created for the app. Back up first if you might need the data.

## A default app: `cipi use` 

Working on one app for a while? Set it once and leave the name out.

```bash
$ cipi use shop
$ cipi deploy            # → shop (default app — cipi use)
$ cipi app logs --type=php
$ cipi use --clear
```

It is stored on the server; `CIPI_APP=shop` sets it for one shell only. For safety, destructive commands (`app delete`, password resets, `convert`, `clone`, `db …`) always require the name, and commands that mean "all apps" without a name keep that meaning.

## Clone an app 

Make a staging or review copy of a Laravel app with its own domain, user and (optionally) a fresh database.

```bash
$ cipi app clone myapp --domain=staging.myapp.com --name=myapp-stg \
    --branch=develop --env=staging --with-db
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--domain` | Required. The clone's domain |
| `--name` | Linux user for the clone |
| `--branch` / `--env` | Deploy branch and environment (default: the source's) |
| `--with-db` / `--no-db` | Create a fresh database, or none |

> [!security] A clone never talks to production by accident: it gets its own Reverb credentials, its own search key and prefix (production search keys are not copied), and no webhook or Git IDs from the source.

## Repair permissions 

```bash
$ cipi app fix-permissions myapp   # one app
$ cipi app fix-permissions         # every app
```

Restores the layout Cipi created, after an archive unpacked as root or a careless `chmod`:

| Path | Mode | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | `750` | Nginx (in the app group) can read; other apps cannot |
| `.ssh` | `700` | SSH refuses a deploy key with looser permissions |
| `shared/.env` | `640` | Secrets readable by the app only |
| `logs/` | `2775` setgid | Nginx writes logs as `www-data` |
| `storage/` | `775` | Laravel writes cache and uploads |

Also available as a button in the [web panel](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-overview).


## Environment variables

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/environment

Each Laravel app has one `.env` at `/home/myapp/shared/.env`, linked into every release, so it survives deploys and rollbacks. Cipi writes it at creation with every credential; you add your own keys.

## Edit 

```bash
$ cipi app env myapp                          # opens it in nano, as the app user
$ cipi app env myapp --show [--json]
$ cipi app env myapp --get=APP_URL
$ cipi app env myapp --set=APP_DEBUG=false
$ cipi app env myapp --unset=LEGACY_KEY
$ cipi worker restart myapp                   # after changing queue or cache drivers
```

New requests read the change immediately (Octane apps: reload on next deploy or `cipi worker restart`). Also via REST (`GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/env`) and MCP. Custom apps have no `.env`.

## What Cipi writes 

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `APP_KEY` | Generated once at creation |
| `APP_URL` | The domain; switched to `https://` by `cipi ssl install` |
| `APP_ENV`, `CIPI_ENV` | The environment label (`production` by default) |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `mysql` (MariaDB) or `pgsql` |
| `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` | The app's own database credentials |
| `CACHE_STORE`, `SESSION_DRIVER`, `QUEUE_CONNECTION` | `database`: isolated per app |
| `REDIS_HOST`, `REDIS_PORT`, `REDIS_PASSWORD` | The app's own Valkey instance, ready when you switch drivers |
| `BROADCAST_CONNECTION`, `REVERB_*`, `VITE_REVERB_*` | Set by `cipi app reverb enable` |
| `CIPI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` | Secret that signs deploy webhooks |
| `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH` | Only pushes to this branch deploy |
| `CIPI_APP_USER` | The app's Linux user |
| `CIPI_MCP` | `true`/`false`: the app's MCP endpoint |

> [!warning] Change database passwords with `cipi app reset-db-password myapp`, never by hand: it updates the database and `.env` together.

Your own keys (Stripe, mail, APIs) go anywhere in the file and are never overwritten by a deploy.

## In the web panel 

Edit the `.env` with secrets masked and changes tracked. The [web panel](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui) is optional; everything here also works from the CLI.


## Queues & Horizon

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/workers

Every Laravel app starts with one Supervisor worker on the `default` queue. Add queues, scale processes, or hand everything to Horizon.

```bash
$ cipi worker add myapp --queue=emails --processes=3
$ cipi worker add myapp --queue=exports --processes=1 --timeout=7200
$ cipi worker edit myapp --queue=default --processes=3
$ cipi worker list myapp
$ cipi worker remove myapp emails
$ cipi worker restart myapp
```

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--queue` | Queue to consume | `default` |
| `--processes` | Parallel processes | 1 |
| `--timeout` | Seconds before a job is killed | 60 |

## Horizon 

```bash
$ cipi worker horizon enable myapp
$ cipi worker horizon status myapp
$ cipi worker horizon disable myapp
```

Horizon replaces the `queue:work` workers of that app (one or the other, not both). It needs the queues on Redis: set `QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis` with [cipi app env](https://cipi.sh/docs/environment); each app has its own [Valkey](https://cipi.sh/docs/valkey) instance ready.

When a deploy finds `laravel/horizon` installed, it helps without overriding your choices:

| The deploy finds | It does |
| --- | --- |
| Horizon, queues on Redis, no worker | Enables Horizon |
| Horizon plus existing workers | Explains how to switch; changes nothing |
| Horizon, queues not on Redis | Tells you which variable to set |

A Horizon you disabled stays disabled. `cipi pending` lists apps with Horizon installed but nothing processing jobs.

## During deploys 

```flow
Stop workers | before the symlink swap
Swap release | atomic
Restart workers | on the new code
```

Workers never run old code against a new database. Supervisor restarts a worker only after an unexpected exit. Workers can also be declared in [cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml).

## As the app user 

App users manage their own workers without root, through a narrow helper:

```bash
$ sudo cipi-worker status myapp
$ sudo cipi-worker restart myapp
```


## Scheduler & cron

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/scheduler

Every Laravel app runs `schedule:run` every minute, as its own user, with its own PHP version. You only turn it on or off.

```bash
$ cipi schedule status myapp
$ cipi schedule off myapp
$ cipi schedule on myapp
```

## Your own cron jobs 

The scheduler lives in the app user's crontab, next to any job you add. Edit it as the app user, so jobs run with the app's permissions:

```bash
$ su - myapp
$ crontab -e
```

```bash
# Laravel scheduler (managed by Cipi, keep it)
* * * * * /usr/bin/php8.6 /home/myapp/current/artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1
# your job, every 15 minutes
*/15 * * * * /home/myapp/current/scripts/sync.sh >> /home/myapp/logs/sync.log 2>&1
```

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the `schedule:run` line | If removed, `cipi schedule on myapp` puts it back |
| Write only inside `/home/myapp` | Jobs have the app's permissions, nothing more |
| Prefer Laravel's scheduler | Jobs stay in code, deployed and versioned with the app |
| Root jobs go in root's crontab | Never give an app more rights than it needs |

## Check it runs 

```bash
$ cipi app artisan myapp schedule:list
$ grep CRON /var/log/syslog | grep myapp | tail -20
```


## Reverb WebSockets

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/reverb

Laravel Reverb is Laravel's own WebSocket server. Cipi runs it behind the app's own domain and certificate: no extra port to open, no second certificate, no credentials to invent.

```bash
$ cipi app reverb enable myapp
$ cipi app reverb status myapp
$ cipi app reverb disable myapp
```

## What enable sets up 

```flow
Browser | wss://myapp.com/app/{key}
Nginx | same domain, same certificate
Reverb on 127.0.0.1 | port 9000–9099
Supervisor | myapp-reverb, as the app user
```

| Piece | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Port | A free local port; Reverb never listens publicly |
| Process | `artisan reverb:start` under Supervisor; log in `~/logs/reverb.log` |
| Nginx | Proxies only `/app/{key}` (handshake) and `/apps/{id}/…` (broadcast API) |
| `.env` | `REVERB_*` credentials generated once and never rotated, plus `VITE_REVERB_*` for the front-end |
| Limits | 65 535 open files for Supervisor and Nginx, so thousands of clients can stay connected |

Running `enable` again is safe: it keeps port and credentials, re-derives host and scheme, and fills in missing keys. Laravel apps only.

## End to end 

```bash
# in your project, then commit
$ composer require laravel/reverb && php artisan install:broadcasting
# on the server
$ cipi app reverb enable myapp
$ cipi ssl install myapp        # wss:// instead of ws://
$ cipi deploy myapp             # Vite bakes VITE_REVERB_* into the bundle
```

The stock `resources/js/echo.js` reads exactly the variables Cipi writes; nothing to change. **Redeploy after a domain or certificate change** so the bundle picks up the new values.

## ws:// or wss:// 

| The app has | Clients use |
| --- | --- |
| No certificate | `ws://` on port 80 |
| A certificate | `wss://` on port 443 |
| A wildcard domain | A concrete host (e.g. `www.example.com`); browsers can't open a socket to `*` |

## Status and troubleshooting 

```bash
$ cipi app reverb status myapp
 Reverb: enabled 127.0.0.1:9000
 myapp-reverb RUNNING pid 21847, uptime 3 days
 Clients dial: wss://myapp.com:443/app/3f9c1ab27de40518b6c4
 Open files: 65535 (supervisor)
```

| Warning | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Missing in .env: …` | Run `cipi app reverb enable myapp` again |
| Certificate present but scheme `http` | `enable` again, then deploy |
| Default open-file limit | `systemctl restart supervisor` (restarts all workers) or enable with `--restart-supervisor` |

> [!warning] `/app` and `/apps` belong to the WebSocket protocol. An app with its own `/app` or `/apps` routes should run Reverb on a separate subdomain.

## Disable, clone, cipi.yml 

`disable` removes the process and the proxy rule and restores the previous broadcast driver (or `log`); credentials stay for a later re-enable. A [clone](https://cipi.sh/docs/manage-apps#cli-app-clone) gets its own port, credentials and host, never production's. In the repository:

```yaml
workers:
  reverb: true
```


## Limits & suspension

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/limits

Cap what one app can use, so a busy or misbehaving app cannot starve the others.

```bash
$ cipi app limits myapp                                   # show
$ cipi app limits myapp --fpm-max-children=20 --memory-limit=256M
$ cipi app limits myapp --octane-workers=4 --worker-procs=3
$ cipi app limits myapp --disk=10                          # soft limit, GB
$ cipi app limits myapp --disk=none
```

| Flag | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| `--fpm-max-children` | Maximum PHP-FPM processes (FPM apps) |
| `--memory-limit` | PHP `memory_limit` |
| `--octane-workers` | Octane workers (Octane apps) |
| `--worker-procs` | Queue worker processes |
| `--disk` | Soft disk limit for files + database, in GB, or `none` |

## Soft disk limit 

No app has one unless you set it. It never blocks the app: it drives the [monitor](https://cipi.sh/docs/monitor).

| Usage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Below 90% | Nothing |
| 90% of the limit | Warning |
| Over the limit | Critical alert, repeated every 4 hours |
| Back under | Recovery notice |

`cipi disk` shows usage next to the limit. The limit is kept outside `cipi.yml` on purpose: **a repository cannot raise the space its server grants it**. Also via REST (`GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/limits`) and the panel.

## Suspend an app 

Take an app offline without deleting anything: for unpaid invoices, maintenance or a staging site you want dark.

```bash
$ cipi app suspend myapp
$ cipi app unsuspend myapp
```

| While suspended | |
| --- | --- |
| Every request | A static **503** page; PHP never runs |
| HTTPS | Covered too |
| Certificate renewals | Keep working |
| Vhost changes (aliases, PHP, SSL) | Respect the suspension |
| `cipi app list`, `cipi domains` | Mark the app as suspended |

Also from the REST API (`POST /api/apps/{name}/suspend`), cipi-cli and the [WHMCS module](https://cipi.sh/docs/whmcs).

> [!tip] Need a private preview instead of a closed site? Use [basic auth](https://cipi.sh/docs/basic-auth): the app runs, behind a password.


## Basic auth

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/basic-auth

Put any app behind a username and password at the Nginx level: staging sites, internal tools, previews for a client.

```bash
$ cipi basicauth enable myapp                          # generates credentials, shown once
$ cipi basicauth enable myapp --user=client --password='…'
$ cipi basicauth status myapp
$ cipi basicauth disable myapp
```

| Property | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | Every path of the app, HTTP and HTTPS |
| Storage | Hashed (APR1) in `/etc/nginx/cipi-basicauth/myapp.htpasswd` |
| Certificates | ACME challenges stay public, so renewals never break |
| Durability | Survives alias, PHP and SSL changes; removed with the app |

Not to be confused with `cipi auth`, which manages Composer credentials for private packages ([Git providers](https://cipi.sh/docs/git#cli-auth)).


## Artisan, commands & logs

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/artisan-logs

Run commands as the app user, with the app's PHP version and restrictions, exactly as a deploy would. No need to switch users.

```bash
$ cipi app artisan myapp migrate:status
$ cipi app artisan myapp queue:retry all
$ cipi app artisan myapp cache:clear
$ cipi app tinker myapp
```

## Other commands: `cipi app run` 

A safe, non-interactive runner used by the CLI, the API and the panel's "App commands".

```bash
$ cipi app run myapp composer install --no-dev
$ cipi app run myapp npm ci
$ cipi app run myapp ls -la shared
$ cipi app run --commands          # what is allowed
```

| Allowed | Blocked |
| --- | --- |
| `composer`, `npm`, `npx`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, `php`, `node`, `git`, `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `find`, archive and file tools | Shells, editors, pagers, REPLs (`bash`, `vim`, `less`, `tinker`), and interactive flags (`tail -f`, `php -a`) |

REST: `POST /api/apps/{name}/run` (ability `apps-run`). MCP: `AppRun`.

## Logs 

```bash
$ cipi app logs myapp                  # everything
$ cipi app logs myapp --type=laravel   # storage/logs/laravel.log
$ cipi app logs myapp --type=nginx     # access and errors
$ cipi app logs myapp --type=php       # PHP-FPM errors
$ cipi app logs myapp --type=worker    # queue workers
$ cipi app logs myapp --type=deploy    # every deploy, timestamped
```

Laravel writes a single `laravel.log` (`LOG_CHANNEL=single`); logrotate rotates it daily, compresses it and keeps a year, like every other app log. See [Log retention](https://cipi.sh/docs/log-retention).


## SSH as the app user

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/app-ssh

Each app is its own Linux user. Log in as that user to inspect files, run scripts or connect an SFTP client, with exactly the app's permissions.

| Path | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `ssh myapp@server` | SFTP, IDE remote sessions, terminal. Password from the creation summary |
| `ssh cipi@server` → `su root` → `su - myapp` | Admin path, when app logins are disabled |

```bash
$ ssh myapp@your-server-ip
myapp@server:~$ cd ~/current
myapp@server:~$ php artisan about
myapp@server:~$ tail -f ~/logs/*.log
myapp@server:~$ ll ~/releases/
```

The app's shell has `ll`, `deploy` and `composer` shortcuts.

## Control access 

```bash
$ cipi app reset-password myapp           # new password, shown once
$ cipi ssh apps disable myapp             # no password logins for this app
$ cipi ssh apps disable --all             # for every app, present and future
```

Disabling app logins does not affect deploys or the admin path. See [SSH keys](https://cipi.sh/docs/ssh-keys#cli-ssh-apps).

> [!note] `open_basedir` confines the app's PHP to `/home/myapp`. Your shell session follows normal file permissions instead.


## How deploys work

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/how-deploys-work

Every deploy runs the same pipeline on the server. What changes is **who starts it**: a push to Git, your CI, you, the panel or an AI agent.

```flow
Trigger | push, CI, CLI, panel, MCP
Build release | clone, composer, assets
Migrate | optional DB snapshot first
Swap symlink | atomic, zero downtime
Verify | health check, auto rollback
```

## Choose a trigger 

| | Push to deploy (webhook) | CI/CD pipeline over SSH |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starts when | You push to the app's branch | Your pipeline's deploy job runs |
| CI needs server access | No: only HTTPS to the app | Yes: a dedicated SSH key as a CI secret |
| Tests before deploy | Separate (the push deploys anyway) | Built in: deploy only if tests pass |
| Setup | One webhook, created for you | SSH key, secrets, workflow file |
| Best for | Most apps | Gated releases, backups, review apps |

| You want… | Use | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Push `main`, it's live | Webhook | [Auto-deploy on push](https://cipi.sh/docs/auto-deploy) |
| Deploy only if tests pass | Pipeline (turn the webhook off) | [CI/CD pipelines](https://cipi.sh/docs/ci-pipelines) |
| Backup before every release | Pipeline, or the built-in snapshot | [Safe deploy](https://cipi.sh/docs/safe-deploy) |
| A live URL per branch | Pipeline | [Preview environments](https://cipi.sh/docs/preview-environments) |
| Slack/Telegram on every deploy | Either | [Deploy notifications](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-notifications) |

> [!warning] **One trigger per app.** A webhook and a pipeline deploying the same push will collide on the deploy lock.


## Deploy & roll back

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/deploying

A deploy builds the new release next to the live one and switches traffic with a single atomic symlink. Visitors never see a half-deployed app, and the previous five releases stay ready for an instant rollback.

## The pipeline 

```flow
Stop workers | no old code on new data
Clone | into releases/N
Composer | --no-dev, app's PHP
Link shared | .env, storage
Migrate & optimize | migrate --force, optimize
Swap | current → releases/N
Restart & verify | workers, health check
```

Deployer and Composer always use **the app's PHP version**, whatever started the deploy. Old releases beyond the last five are pruned. Octane apps reload Octane; apps with a [front-end build](https://cipi.sh/docs/manage-apps#edit) run it before the swap.

## Commands 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi deploy myapp` | Deploy the latest commit of the branch |
| `cipi deploy myapp --rollback` | Back to the previous release, instantly |
| `cipi deploy myapp --status` | Is a deploy running, queued or interrupted? (safe to poll) |
| `cipi deploy myapp --history` | Past deploys and rollbacks: result, release, duration, trigger |
| `cipi deploy --last` | The last deploy of every app |
| `cipi deploy myapp --releases` | Releases on disk with date, duration, commit |
| `cipi deploy myapp --log=200` | Timestamped deploy log |
| `cipi deploy myapp --audit` | Who deployed what, from where ([audit ledger](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-audit)) |
| `cipi deploy myapp --snapshot` | Dump the database first ([safe deploy](https://cipi.sh/docs/safe-deploy)) |
| `cipi deploy myapp --rollback-on-unhealthy` | Undo the release if the [health check](https://cipi.sh/docs/health-checks) fails |
| `cipi deploy myapp --key` / `--webhook` | Show the deploy key / webhook URL and token |
| `cipi deploy myapp --unlock` | Clear the lock of an interrupted deploy |
| `cipi deploy myapp --trust-host=git.example.com:2222` | Trust a self-hosted Git server |

## Know whether it worked 

| Signal | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Exit code | Non-zero on failure, so CI and scripts can react |
| Email / alerts | Success and failure, with branch, release, commit, author, duration and health verdict ([notifications](https://cipi.sh/docs/notifications)) |
| Log | `~/logs/deploy.log`: every line timestamped, each run framed by trigger, branch, release and duration |
| History | `--history` reads rotated logs too, so last month's webhook deploy still shows how long it took |

The success notice is sent only **after** the post-deploy health check, so it never announces a release that returns errors.

## Status values 

| `--status` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `running` | Building (`deploy`) or verifying (`post-deploy`); shows trigger, branch and elapsed time |
| `queued` | A push arrived; the deploy starts within a minute |
| `interrupted` | The process died (reboot, kill); clear with `--unlock` |
| `idle` | Nothing running; shows how the last run ended |

A failed deploy releases its own lock; only an interrupted one needs `--unlock`.

## In the web panel 

Deploy, follow the release and read the audit from the browser. The [web panel](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui) is optional; everything here also works from the CLI.


## Git providers & deploy keys

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/git

Cipi reads the repository with a per-app **read-only SSH deploy key** and deploys on push through a **signed webhook**. With a provider token, both are created, rotated and removed for you.

## Supported providers 

The provider is recognised from the SSH clone URL.

| Provider | Deploy key | Push webhook |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | Automatic | Automatic, HMAC-signed |
| GitLab (cloud or self-hosted) | Automatic | Automatic, secret token |
| Bitbucket Cloud | Automatic | Automatic, HMAC-signed |
| Azure DevOps | Automatic | Automatic (service hook) |
| Cursor Origin | Automatic | None: deploy with `cipi deploy` or CI |
| AWS CodeCommit | Automatic (IAM RSA key) | None: deploy with `cipi deploy` or CI |
| Anything else (Gitea, Forgejo…) | Manual | Manual |

No lock-in: any server that accepts SSH deploy keys works.

## Save a token 

The installer offers this step; you can also do it any time:

```bash
$ cipi git github-token ghp_xxx
$ cipi git gitlab-url https://gitlab.example.com   # self-hosted only
$ cipi git gitlab-token glpat-xxx
$ cipi git bitbucket-token                  # or email:token
$ cipi git azure-token 
$ cipi git origin-token 
$ cipi git codecommit-token   
$ cipi git remove-github                           # remove-gitlab, -bitbucket, …
```

| Provider | Minimum permissions |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub | Fine-grained: Administration + Webhooks, read & write. Classic: `repo` |
| GitLab | `api` |
| Bitbucket | Manage repository access keys and webhooks |
| Azure DevOps | Code (read & write) |
| CodeCommit | IAM `UploadSSHPublicKey` (max 5 SSH keys per IAM user) |

Tokens are stored encrypted on the server ([Vault](https://cipi.sh/docs/vault)).

## What happens automatically 

| Event | Cipi |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi app create` | Adds the deploy key and webhook, then **tests** that the key can read the branch |
| `cipi app edit --repository=` | Removes them from the old repository, adds them to the new one, tests again |
| `cipi app delete` | Removes them from the repository |

| Command | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi git status` | Connected providers and per-app key/webhook IDs |
| `cipi git check [app]` | Can each key read its repository and branch? Exits 1 if not |
| `cipi git refresh [app]` | Re-create keys and webhooks (after deletions or a new token) |
| `cipi git refresh --rotate-keys` | New deploy keys for every app |
| `cipi git refresh --rotate-secret` | New webhook secrets |

## Manual setup 

Without a token, or for an unsupported server:

```bash
$ cipi deploy myapp --key                          # add as a read-only deploy key
$ cipi deploy myapp --webhook                      # payload URL and secret
$ cipi deploy myapp --trust-host=git.example.com:2222   # self-hosted, custom port
```

> [!note] With [CrowdSec](https://cipi.sh/docs/crowdsec) enabled, GitHub and Bitbucket webhook ranges are allowlisted automatically. For other providers, allow a blocked range with `cipi crowdsec allow `.

## Private packages: auth.json 

`shared/auth.json` is linked into every release like `.env`, so Composer finds credentials for private packages (Packagist.com, Satis, GitHub) on every deploy.

```bash
$ cipi auth create myapp      # creates it (mode 640) and opens the editor
$ cipi auth edit myapp        # JSON is validated on save
$ cipi auth show myapp
$ cipi auth delete myapp
```

Non-interactive flags (`--file=`, `--json`, `--force`) serve scripts and the panel; REST `GET|POST|PUT|DELETE /api/apps/{name}/auth`.


## Auto-deploy on push

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/auto-deploy

Push to your branch and the app is live a minute later. The Git provider calls a signed webhook on your app; the deploy itself runs on the server as the app user. CI needs no SSH key and the server opens no extra port.

## How it works 

```flow
git push | to the deploy branch
Provider → /cipi/webhook | signed request over HTTPS
Verify & queue | signature, branch; answers 200 at once
Cron, within a minute | starts the deploy as the app user
Deploy | the normal zero-downtime pipeline
```

The webhook only drops a trigger file; it never runs the deploy itself. That keeps the HTTP answer instant (providers time out after ~10 s) and the deploy in the same safe context as `cipi deploy`.

| Receiver | Used by | Verifies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Cipi Agent](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent-install) (`cipi/agent`) | Laravel apps | GitHub/Bitbucket HMAC, GitLab/Azure token, Gitea/Forgejo signature |
| Built-in receiver | Node apps | GitHub/Bitbucket HMAC, GitLab/Azure token |

## Set it up 

```bash
# in your Laravel project
$ composer require cipi/agent && git commit -am "Add Cipi Agent" && git push
# on the server: one manual deploy, so the route exists
$ cipi deploy myapp
$ cipi git status                 # webhook already created?
$ cipi deploy myapp --webhook     # if not: URL and secret to add by hand
```

| Provider | Payload URL | Secret | Events |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | `https://myapp.com/cipi/webhook` | the token from `--webhook` | push |
| GitLab | same | Secret token: same value | Push events |

Only pushes to `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH` deploy; others get `skipped`. Cipi keeps it in step with `cipi app edit --branch`. Use HTTPS ([cipi ssl install](https://cipi.sh/docs/ssl)) so the secret never travels in clear text.

Verify with a small commit:

```bash
$ cipi deploy myapp --status
$ cipi app logs myapp --type=deploy
```

Every webhook deploy lands in the [audit ledger](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-audit) with pusher, commit, delivery ID and source IP.

## Troubleshooting 

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | Agent not deployed yet | `cipi deploy myapp` after adding `cipi/agent` |
| 403, invalid signature | Secret mismatch | Copy the token from `cipi deploy myapp --webhook` again |
| 200 but no deploy | Another branch was pushed | Check `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH` |
| Lock error | An interrupted deploy | `cipi deploy myapp --unlock` |
| Two deploys per push | Webhook and pipeline both active | Keep [one trigger](https://cipi.sh/docs/how-deploys-work) |


## CI/CD pipelines

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/ci-pipelines

Use a pipeline when a deploy must be **conditional**: only after tests pass, after a backup, with a notification, or to create a review app per branch. The pipeline SSHs into the server and runs `cipi deploy`. Turn the app's webhook off so only the pipeline deploys.

```flow
Push | to main
Test | php artisan test
Backup | optional
Deploy | ssh → cipi deploy
Notify / roll back | on failure
```

## A key for CI 

Create a dedicated key; never reuse a personal key or a deploy key.

```bash
$ ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ci-deploy" -f ~/.ssh/ci_deploy -N ""
$ cat ~/.ssh/ci_deploy.pub   # on the server: sudo cipi ssh add ""
$ cat ~/.ssh/ci_deploy       # → CI secret SERVER_SSH_KEY
```

Store `SERVER_SSH_KEY` and `SERVER_HOST` as secrets. The `cipi` user runs only `sudo cipi …` without a password, so the CI key cannot do anything else as root. See [SSH keys](https://cipi.sh/docs/ssh-keys).

## GitHub Actions 

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
name: Deploy
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: composer install && php artisan test
  deploy:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.SERVER_HOST }}
          username: cipi
          key: ${{ secrets.SERVER_SSH_KEY }}
          script: sudo cipi deploy myapp || (sudo cipi deploy myapp --rollback && exit 1)
```

## GitLab CI 

```yaml
# .gitlab-ci.yml
stages: [test, deploy]
test:
  stage: test
  script: [composer install, php artisan test]
deploy:
  stage: deploy
  only: [main]
  before_script:
    - eval $(ssh-agent -s) && echo "$SERVER_SSH_KEY" | tr -d '\r' | ssh-add -
    - mkdir -p ~/.ssh && ssh-keyscan -H $SERVER_HOST >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
  script:
    - ssh cipi@$SERVER_HOST "sudo cipi deploy myapp || (sudo cipi deploy myapp --rollback && exit 1)"
```

## Several apps from one pipeline 

```bash
$ sudo cipi deploy frontend & sudo cipi deploy api & wait
```

## Build on it 

| Add | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Backup before release | [Safe deploy](https://cipi.sh/docs/safe-deploy) |
| Slack/Telegram on success or failure | [Deploy notifications](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-notifications) |
| A live app per branch | [Preview environments](https://cipi.sh/docs/preview-environments) |

> [!tip] A common setup: webhook for staging (instant feedback), pipeline for production (tests → backup → deploy → notify).


## cipi.yml

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/yml

`cipi.yml` describes, in your repository, how the server should run the app: aliases, PHP settings, databases, workers, scheduler, health check, backups, routes, deploy options, crons. Server configuration gets reviewed, versioned and deployed like code.

```flow
Commit cipi.yml | next to your code
Deploy | the file ships with the release
Plan | see exactly what would change
Apply | all or nothing, never half
```

## Commands 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi yml generate myapp [--save]` | Write the app's current setup as a ready-to-commit file |
| `cipi yml example myapp` | A commented template that validates as is |
| `cipi yml validate myapp` | Parse and check; change nothing |
| `cipi yml plan myapp [--json]` | Show every change that would be made |
| `cipi yml apply myapp [--yes]` | Apply it |
| `cipi yml auto myapp on\|off\|status` | Apply automatically after every successful deploy |
| `cipi yml post-deploy myapp` | Run the `deploy.post` steps now |

Start from what you have: `cipi yml generate myapp > cipi.yml`, commit, and `plan` reports nothing to do. Validate locally or in CI with [Cipi Agent](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent-yml): `php artisan cipi:yml validate`.

The file is read from the live release (`current/` or, for custom apps, `htdocs/`), then `shared/`. Every vhost refuses to serve it.

## The file 

```yaml
version: 1

app:
  php: "8.6"                       # must be installed
  aliases: ["www.myapp.com", "*.myapp.com"]   # replaces the current list
  ini: { upload_max_filesize: 50M, memory_limit: 512M }
  limits: { memory_limit: 512M, fpm_max_children: 10 }

databases:                         # extra databases: myapp or myapp_*
  - name: myapp_reporting
  - name: myapp_analytics
    engine: pgsql

workers:
  horizon: false                   # true replaces the queues below
  reverb: false
  queues:
    - { queue: default, processes: 2 }
    - { queue: emails, processes: 1, tries: 5, timeout: 300 }

schedule: true
search: false                      # Meilisearch for Scout

health:
  url: "https://myapp.com/up"      # must be one of the app's domains
  expect: 200
  rollback_on_unhealthy: true

deploy:
  branch: main
  keep_releases: 5
  predeploy_snapshot: true
  node_build: "npm ci && npm run build"
  post:
    - artisan cache:clear

ssl: { force_https: true }
env: { required: [STRIPE_KEY, MAIL_HOST] }   # names only, never values

crons:
  - { every: 30m, run: artisan queue:prune-batches }

backup:
  profiles:                        # names: myapp or myapp-*
    - { name: myapp-db, scope: db, every: 30m, keep: 48, destinations: [local] }
    - { name: myapp-nightly, scope: all, cron: "0 2 * * *", keep_days: 14, destinations: [s3], encrypt: true }
```

| Section | Same as | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.php`, `app.ini` | [cipi php / ini](https://cipi.sh/docs/php) | Per-app; server-wide ini stays with `cipi ini` |
| `app.aliases` | [cipi alias](https://cipi.sh/docs/domains) | Authoritative: a removed alias is removed |
| `app.limits` | [cipi app limits](https://cipi.sh/docs/limits) | Out-of-range values block the plan instead of being clamped |
| `databases` | [cipi db](https://cipi.sh/docs/databases) | Credentials go to `shared/cipi-databases.env`, never to the repo |
| `workers`, `schedule` | [Queues](https://cipi.sh/docs/workers), [Reverb](https://cipi.sh/docs/reverb), [Scheduler](https://cipi.sh/docs/scheduler) | Laravel apps only |
| `search` | [cipi search](https://cipi.sh/docs/search) | Needs `cipi search install` by root first |
| `health` | [Health checks](https://cipi.sh/docs/health-checks) | Probed every 5 minutes and after every deploy |
| `deploy` | [deploy-config](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-script) | `branch` takes effect from the next deploy |
| `ssl.force_https` | `cipi ssl force` | Can only be turned on from the file |
| `env.required` | | A missing variable blocks the plan |
| `crons` | | Allowlisted runners only; your other cron lines are untouched |
| `backup.profiles` | [cipi backup](https://cipi.sh/docs/backups) | The file owns the profiles it created |

## Routes: www, basic auth, redirects, proxies 

```yaml
app:
  aliases: ["www.myapp.com"]
  www: to-root                     # to-root | from-root | none
  basic_auth:
    users:
      - admin                      # keeps the password set on the server
      - { name: preview, password_hash: "$2y$12$…" }   # bcrypt or SHA-512 only
redirect: { to: "https://new.example.com", code: 301, keep_path: true }
redirects:
  - { from: /old-page, to: /new-page }
  - { from: /blog/, to: "https://blog.myapp.com/", code: 308 }
proxies:
  - { prefix: /api/, upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:3000", strip_prefix: true }
```

Routes apply as one change: one vhost rewrite, one `nginx -t`, reverted as a whole if Nginx refuses it. **No passwords in the repository**: users are names or strong hashes.

## Staging and production from one repository 

Each app has an environment label (`production` by default; set with `--env` on create, clone or edit). An app reads `cipi-.yml` first and falls back to `cipi.yml`.

| File | Read by | Typically |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cipi-staging.yml` | apps with `--env=staging` | `deploy: { branch: develop }` |
| `cipi.yml` (or `cipi-production.yml`) | production apps | `deploy: { branch: main }` |

```bash
$ cipi app clone shop --domain=staging.shop.com --name=shop-stg --env=staging
$ cipi yml plan shop-stg     # deploy branch: main → develop (from the next deploy)
```

The **server** decides which file an app reads, never the file itself: a commit cannot point production at the staging file. An invalid `cipi-.yml` does not fall back silently; the error names it.

## Node apps: `node:` 

```yaml
node:
  framework: next                  # next nuxt sveltekit astro remix vite
  mode: ssr                        # spa | static | ssr
  version: 22
  start: npx next start -H 127.0.0.1
```

Applied by the deploy itself, from the release being deployed, so the commit that changes the build is built with it. Requires `cipi yml auto myapp on`.

## Post-deploy steps: `deploy.post` 

Commands run from the live release after every successful deploy, webhook included. They need no auto-apply.

```yaml
deploy:
  post:
    - artisan scout:import --force
    - composer dump-autoload -o
    - node scripts/warm-cache.mjs
    - { run: artisan, command: view:cache }
  post_on_failure: warn            # or abort: cipi deploy fails too
```

| Allowed runners | Refused |
| --- | --- |
| `artisan`, `composer`, `npm`, `npx`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, `php`/`node` + a script inside the release | shells, pipes, `;`, `..`, `artisan tinker`, unknown commands |

Order of a deploy: build → swap → `cipi yml apply` (if auto) → `deploy.post` → health check → notification.

## Auto-apply 

Nothing on the server changes from the file until you run `cipi yml auto myapp on`. Then every successful deploy (CLI, panel, API or webhook) reconciles. A release without the file is a no-op; an invalid or blocked file is reported (`yml_fail`) and **never partially applied**, and the deploy itself still succeeds.

## Why it is safe to accept over Git 

Anyone who can push controls the file, so it is fail-closed:

| Guard | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Configure only | It can never create, rename or delete an app |
| Namespaced | Databases and backup profiles must belong to the app |
| Own domains only | The health check can't aim the server at internal addresses |
| No shell | Only allowlisted runners; unknown keys are errors |
| Small YAML subset | Anchors, aliases, tags, merges and block scalars are refused |
| Strict proxies | Cipi's own ports, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused |
| Server-only settings | Disk limit and which environment file is read can't be changed from the file |

> [!warning] With auto-apply on, push access to the repository means control over this app's configuration. Treat write access accordingly.


## Customize the pipeline

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-script

Most apps never touch the deploy recipe: the options below cover the common needs and are kept safely across updates. For anything else, add your own Deployer tasks.

## Deploy options 

```bash
$ cipi app deploy-config myapp                                  # show
$ cipi app deploy-config myapp --keep-releases=10
$ cipi app deploy-config myapp --no-migrate --no-optimize
$ cipi app deploy-config myapp --horizon-terminate --queue-restart
$ cipi app deploy-config myapp --extra-artisan=view:clear,event:cache
$ cipi app deploy-config myapp --node-build='npm ci && npm run build'
$ cipi app deploy-config myapp --predeploy-snapshot
```

| Option | Effect | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--keep-releases` | Releases kept for rollback | 5 |
| `--migrate` / `--no-migrate` | `migrate --force` | on |
| `--optimize` / `--no-optimize` | `artisan optimize` | on |
| `--storage-link` | `storage:link` | on |
| `--queue-restart`, `--horizon-terminate` | Reload workers / Horizon | on |
| `--extra-artisan` | More Artisan commands after migrations | none |
| `--node-build` | Front-end build before the swap (npm, yarn, pnpm, bun) | none |
| `--predeploy-snapshot` | Database dump before migrations | off |

Saving regenerates `deploy.php` from Cipi's template. Also via REST (`GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/deploy-config`), MCP and the panel's Deploy tab. The same settings can live in [cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml).

## Custom Deployer tasks 

The recipe is `/home/myapp/.deployer/deploy.php`. Add tasks **at the bottom**, below the Cipi-managed blocks:

```php
// ── Custom tasks (keep below Cipi-managed blocks) ──
task('app:warm', function () {
    run('{{bin/php}} {{release_path}}/artisan app:warm-cache');
});
after('artisan:migrate', 'app:warm');
```

| Hook point | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `after('deploy:shared', …)` | Builds that need `.env` (e.g. Vite reads `VITE_*`) |
| `after('artisan:migrate', …)` | Seeders, cache warm-up |
| `before('deploy:symlink', …)` | Last checks before going live |
| `after('deploy:symlink', …)` | Notifications, cache purges |

The default order: prepare → vendors → shared → (build) → migrate → optimize → storage link → **symlink** → restart workers → cleanup.

> [!warning] Changing PHP or branch with `cipi app edit` regenerates `deploy.php`. Keep custom tasks in one clearly marked block at the bottom and back it up, or prefer `deploy-config` and [cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml), which are never lost.

Test every change with a normal deploy; `cipi deploy myapp --rollback` is always one command away, and the log is in `cipi app logs myapp --type=deploy`.


## Safe deploy & DB snapshots

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/safe-deploy

A safe deploy has a restore point taken **before** new code and migrations touch production. Cipi gives you two levels; use one or both.

| Level | How | Restores | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Database snapshot | `--snapshot` or `--predeploy-snapshot` | The database | On the server |
| Full backup | `cipi backup run` in a pipeline stage | Database + files (`shared/`: `.env`, uploads) | S3 or any S3-compatible bucket |

```flow
Tests pass | CI
Snapshot / backup | restore point
Deploy | atomic swap
Health check | automatic rollback if broken
```

## Database snapshot before every deploy 

```bash
$ cipi deploy shop --snapshot             # dump first; warn and continue if it fails
$ cipi deploy shop --snapshot-required    # dump first; abort the deploy if it fails
$ cipi app edit shop --predeploy-snapshot # always, for every trigger (CLI, webhook, CI)
```

Dumps go to `/var/log/cipi/backups/`, the same place as [cipi db backup](https://cipi.sh/docs/databases).

> [!warning] `cipi deploy --rollback` restores **code**, not data. To undo a migration, restore the snapshot: `cipi db restore shop /var/log/cipi/backups/shop_.sql.gz`.

## Full backup in a pipeline 

A webhook deploys as soon as you push, so an off-site backup step belongs in a [CI pipeline](https://cipi.sh/docs/ci-pipelines). Configure S3 once with `cipi backup configure`.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml (jobs only)
  backup:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.SERVER_HOST }}
          username: cipi
          key: ${{ secrets.SERVER_SSH_KEY }}
          script: sudo cipi db backup shop && sudo cipi backup run --profile=shop-nightly
  deploy:
    needs: backup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.SERVER_HOST }}
          username: cipi
          key: ${{ secrets.SERVER_SSH_KEY }}
          script: sudo cipi deploy shop || (sudo cipi deploy shop --rollback && exit 1)
```

`test` → `backup` → `deploy`: if one fails, the next never runs; if the deploy fails, the previous release is restored.

## Restore 

```bash
$ ls -lh /var/log/cipi/backups/shop_*.sql.gz
$ cipi db restore shop /var/log/cipi/backups/shop_20261103_143012.sql.gz
$ cipi deploy shop --rollback
# from S3
$ cipi backup list --profile=shop-nightly
$ cipi backup fetch shop-nightly 2026-11-03_020000 --dest=/root/restore
```

Local snapshots are kept until you remove them; see [Backups](https://cipi.sh/docs/backups) for retention rules that prune automatically.


## Deploy audit ledger

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-audit

Every deploy, rollback and failure is written to a tamper-evident ledger, whoever started it: the CLI, the panel, a webhook, an AI agent, cron or someone typing `dep deploy` over SSH. Useful for incident reviews and for auditors.

```bash
$ cipi deploy myapp --audit                    # last 90 days
$ cipi deploy myapp --audit --days=365 --json
$ cipi compliance deploys                      # verify the chain, find gaps
```

## What a record proves 

The app's deploy recipe calls a root-owned helper at each outcome. Root **verifies** facts itself instead of trusting the caller:

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Event | `published`, `failed`, `rollback` |
| Release and commit | Read from disk by root |
| Origin | From the process chain: `cipi-cli`, `panel`, `webhook`, `app-queue`, `ssh`, `cron`, `root-shell`… |
| Operator | The login user ID set by PAM (the user can't change it) |
| IP | The SSH client address |
| Claimed | What only the app can say (e.g. who clicked deploy in an MCP client), kept apart from verified facts |

## The ledger 

`/var/log/cipi/deploys.jsonl` is root-only. Each line carries a sequence number and the SHA-256 of the previous line, and is also sent to syslog (`cipi-deploy`), so log forwarding keeps an independent copy off the server.

| `cipi compliance deploys` | When |
| --- | --- |
| **Fails** | The hash chain is broken |
| **Warns** | An app's recipe lost its hook, its sudo rule is missing, or Deployer knows a release the ledger never saw |

The panel shows the ledger on each app's Deploy tab; the API serves it at `GET /api/apps/{name}/deploy/audit`.

> [!note] The chain proves nothing older than the newest record was changed. Root could still rewrite the whole file, which is why the syslog copy matters. File edits over SFTP are not deploys; [malware scan](https://cipi.sh/docs/malware-scan) integrity covers those.


## Preview environments

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/preview-environments

Give every branch its own live URL: a complete app with database, workers and HTTPS, created on the first push and deleted with the branch. Reviewers click a link instead of pulling code.

```flow
Push feature/x | to any non-main branch
CI computes a name | stable per branch
Create or deploy | cipi app create / deploy
Live URL | feature-x-shop-3a1f9c2e.preview.example.com
Branch deleted | app deleted
```

## One-time setup 

| Step | How |
| --- | --- |
| Wildcard DNS | `A *.preview.example.com → server IP` |
| Wildcard certificate | With the Cloudflare token Cipi keeps: `certbot certonly --dns-cloudflare --dns-cloudflare-credentials /etc/cipi/cloudflare.ini -d preview.example.com -d '*.preview.example.com' --cert-name preview.example.com` (renews by itself). Without Cloudflare: [Wildcard domains](https://cipi.sh/docs/wildcard-domains) |
| Repository access | A read-only token (`GH_PAT`, `GL_TOKEN`), so previews need no deploy key |
| CI secrets | `SERVER_HOST`, `SERVER_SSH_KEY`, `DEPLOY_WILDCARD_DOMAIN` |

## The server-side script 

Commit this as `.cipi/preview.sh`; the pipeline sends it over SSH. It creates the app once, adds HTTPS with the wildcard certificate, then deploys.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: preview.sh      
set -euo pipefail
ACTION=$1 APP=$2 DOMAIN=$3 REPO=$4 BRANCH=$5 BASE=$6
CERT=/etc/letsencrypt/live/$BASE
if [ "$ACTION" = down ]; then
  cipi app show "$APP" &>/dev/null && cipi app delete "$APP" --force || true
  exit 0
fi
if ! cipi app show "$APP" &>/dev/null; then
  cipi app create --user="$APP" --domain="$DOMAIN" --repository="$REPO" --branch="$BRANCH"
  awk -v c="$CERT" '/^    listen 80;/{print; print "    listen 443 ssl;"; print "    ssl_certificate " c "/fullchain.pem;"; print "    ssl_certificate_key " c "/privkey.pem;"; next}{print}' \
    "/etc/nginx/sites-available/$APP" > /tmp/vhost && mv /tmp/vhost "/etc/nginx/sites-available/$APP"
  nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx
fi
cipi deploy "$APP"
```

## The pipeline (GitHub Actions) 

```yaml
# .github/workflows/preview.yml
name: Preview
on:
  push: { branches-ignore: [main] }
  delete:
jobs:
  preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: ids
        run: |
          REF="${{ github.event.ref || github.ref_name }}"; REF="${REF#refs/heads/}"
          B=$(echo "$REF" | tr A-Z a-z | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]/-/g; s/--*/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//')
          P=$(echo "${{ github.event.repository.name }}" | tr A-Z a-z | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]/-/g')
          H=$(echo -n "$B$P" | md5sum | cut -c1-8)
          echo "app=pr$H" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "domain=$B-$P-$H.${{ secrets.DEPLOY_WILDCARD_DOMAIN }}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "branch=$REF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.SERVER_SSH_KEY }}" > key && chmod 600 key
          ACTION=${{ github.event_name == 'delete' && 'down' || 'up' }}
          ssh -i key -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new cipi@${{ secrets.SERVER_HOST }} \
            "sudo bash -s -- $ACTION ${{ steps.ids.outputs.app }} ${{ steps.ids.outputs.domain }} \
             https://oauth2:${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}@github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git \
             ${{ steps.ids.outputs.branch }} ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_WILDCARD_DOMAIN }}" ` app user | Valid Linux user, stable for the branch, so re-runs update instead of duplicating |
| `branch-project-hash` domain | Readable and unique |

## Good to know 

> [!warning] Each preview is a full app: user, database, PHP pool, worker. On a small VPS, prune stale ones (`cipi app list`), or keep previews on a dedicated server.

- Write `listen 443 ssl;` (no `http2`), like every vhost Cipi writes; `cipi nginx security` flags vhosts that enable HTTP/2 ([Nginx](https://cipi.sh/docs/nginx)).
- Don't run `cipi ssl install` on a preview: the wildcard certificate already covers it.


## Deploy notifications

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-notifications

Know about every deploy, success or failure, without watching logs. The simplest way is the server itself: it notifies for **every** trigger, webhook deploys included.

## From the server (recommended) 

```bash
$ cipi notification add slack ops --url=https://hooks.slack.com/services/…
$ cipi notification add telegram team --token= --chat-id=
$ cipi notification test
```

| Event | Sent when |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy_success` | After the post-deploy health check passes |
| `deploy_fail` | The deploy failed; the live release is unchanged |
| `deploy_rollback` | A rollback ran (manual or automatic) |

Messages include app, branch, release, commit and author, duration and health verdict. Channels: email (SMTP, Resend, SES), Slack, Discord, Mattermost, Google Chat, Telegram, ntfy, Pushover, signed webhook. See [Notifications](https://cipi.sh/docs/notifications).

## From CI 

When the message should come from the pipeline (with the CI run link), add a step after `cipi deploy`:
