| Origin check | Browser requests from other hosts refused (DNS-rebinding guard) |
| Annotations | Every tool declares read-only/destructive hints so clients can ask before acting |

> [!warning] The MCP token can deploy, read logs and query the database. Keep it secret; rotate with `php artisan cipi:generate-token mcp` (restart Octane and workers after).

## Connect your client 

```json
// Cursor: ~/.cursor/mcp.json
{ "mcpServers": { "cipi-myapp": {
    "type": "http", "url": "https://myapp.com/cipi/mcp",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_CIPI_MCP_TOKEN" } } } }
```

```json
// VS Code: .vscode/mcp.json (token asked once, never committed)
{ "inputs": [{ "type": "promptString", "id": "cipi-token", "description": "Cipi MCP token", "password": true }],
  "servers": { "cipi-myapp": { "type": "http", "url": "https://myapp.com/cipi/mcp",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:cipi-token}" } } } }
```

```bash
# Claude Code
$ claude mcp add --transport http cipi-myapp https://myapp.com/cipi/mcp \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_CIPI_MCP_TOKEN"
```

```json
// Claude Desktop (stdio bridge): claude_desktop_config.json
{ "mcpServers": { "cipi-myapp": { "command": "npx",
    "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://myapp.com/cipi/mcp", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_CIPI_MCP_TOKEN"] } } }
```

## What a session looks like 

```text
You:    Is production healthy, and what commit is live?
Claude: [health, deploy_status] Healthy. Release 20261109103000, commit 0123456 (webhook, 42 s).
You:    Show the last errors and tell me which job fails.
Claude: [logs level=error] InvoiceJob: column invoices.paid_at not found.
        [artisan migrate:status] 2026_11_08_add_paid_at is pending.
You:    Deploy main and note that Jane asked.
Claude: [deploy actor=jane@example.com] Queued; it runs within a minute.
```

## Panel tools 

With [cipi/sdk](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-sdk) and a server API token, the same MCP server gains server-side actions no in-app process could do:

```bash
$ composer require cipi/sdk
# on the server: cipi api token create   (abilities: apps-view, deploy-manage, dbs-manage, status-view)
```

```ini
CIPI_BASE_URL=https://api.myserver.com
CIPI_TOKEN=your-sanctum-token
```

| Tool | Does | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `panel_status` | The app as the panel sees it, plus server snapshot | `apps-view`, `status-view` |
| `panel_deploy_audit` | The hash-chained deploy ledger | `deploy-manage` |
| `panel_rollback` | Roll back the code (migrations stay) | `deploy-manage` |
| `panel_db_backup` | Server-side database snapshot, e.g. before a risky fix | `dbs-manage` |
| `panel_job` | Status and output of an async job | any |

Scope that token to exactly these abilities: it is the one credential that reaches beyond the app.


## cipi.yml tooling

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/agent-yml

The agent ships **the same parser and validator as the server**, so you get the server's verdict, with the same error messages, on your laptop and in CI, before you push. Plus a generator that writes a first `cipi.yml` from your Laravel code.

```bash
$ php artisan cipi:yml validate [--json] [--strict]   # exit 1 on errors
$ php artisan cipi:yml show                            # normalized, with server defaults
$ php artisan cipi:yml generate --write                # inferred from this app
$ php artisan cipi:yml example --write                 # commented template
$ php artisan cipi:yml schema --write                  # JSON Schema for your editor
```

```flow
Generate | from your code
Edit | with schema autocompletion
Validate | locally and in CI
Commit & deploy | server plans and applies
```

## Generate from your app 

`cipi:yml generate` reads the code and proposes a file the server will accept:

| Detected | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `laravel/horizon` or `QUEUE_CONNECTION` | `workers.horizon` or `workers.queues` |
| `laravel/reverb` | `workers.reverb: true` |
| Scout with Meilisearch | `search: true` |
| Scheduled tasks | `schedule: true` |
| `/up` health route | `health.url` |
| `CIPI_PHP_VERSION` | `app.php` |
| Credential-looking keys in `.env.example` | `env.required` |

## Validate in CI 

```bash
$ php artisan cipi:yml validate
INFO cipi.yml is valid (/var/www/shop/cipi.yml)
WARN env.required: STRIPE_KEY is not set in .env — the server blocks the plan while it is missing
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml (step)
      - run: php artisan cipi:yml validate --json --app=shop
```

Every server rule applies: unknown keys, bounds, namespaces for databases and backup profiles, allowlisted runners in `deploy.post`. Outside the server, pass the app name with `--app=` (on the server it's read from `CIPI_APP_USER`). The validator picks `cipi-.yml` first, like the server.

## Editor support 

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./cipi.schema.json
version: 1
```

Completion and inline errors as you type in VS Code, PhpStorm or any YAML language server.

## From your AI assistant 

The MCP `cipi_yml` tool validates a draft passed as `content`, so an assistant can propose a change and hand you a file the server accepts, without writing to your repository. `env_check` lists the `env.required` names missing on the server (never values).

> [!tip] Keep `cipi/agent` up to date: when Cipi learns a new `cipi.yml` key, the agent's validator learns it in the matching release. Until then the server's verdict wins.


## Database anonymizer

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/anonymizer

The anonymizer gives you **a copy of production that looks real but contains no real people**. Developers, QA, staging and contractors get the same tables, volumes and relations, with e-mails, names, phones, addresses and notes replaced by Faker values. MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL are supported.

It lives inside your Laravel app (`cipi/agent`), runs as a queued job, and is safe by construction: the raw dump is deleted as soon as it's processed, outputs are `0600`, database passwords travel in the environment, never on a command line, and the download link expires.

```flow
Request | POST /cipi/db, cipi-cli or Artisan
Queue | AnonymizeDatabaseJob
Dump | mysqldump / pg_dump
Rewrite | only configured columns
Email | signed link, 15 minutes
```

| Use case | Why it fits |
| --- | --- |
| Local development | Realistic data on every laptop, no production e-mails |
| Staging and previews | Production structure and volume, PII replaced |
| QA and demos | Reproduce bugs that depend on real relations, without GDPR risk |
| Contractors | Share a SQL file instead of production access |

## Anonymizer vs backups 

| | Anonymizer (`cipi/agent`) | Backups ([Cipi API](https://cipi.sh/docs/api)) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scope | One Laravel app's database | Any database on the server |
| Output | SQL with fake values in sensitive columns | Full compressed backup, real data |
| Auth | `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TOKEN` (per app) | Sanctum token with `dbs-manage` |
| For | People who need realistic data | Disaster recovery, cloning |

Use both: backups for operations, anonymized dumps for humans.

## Requirements 

| Requirement | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi/agent` installed | The anonymizer is part of the agent |
| A queue worker | `POST /cipi/db` dispatches a job; without a worker nothing runs |
| `mysqldump` / `mariadb-dump` / `pg_dump` | Found on `PATH`, or set `CIPI_MYSQLDUMP` / `CIPI_PG_DUMP` |
| Laravel mail (`MAIL_*`) | The download link only travels by e-mail |
| `anonymization.json` on the server | In `~/.db/` (or `~/.cipi/`), outside the repository |

## Setup 

As the app user on the server ([SSH as the app user](https://cipi.sh/docs/app-ssh)), or remotely with `cipi-cli apps artisan myapp …`:

```bash
$ composer require cipi/agent                   # commit, push, deploy
$ php artisan cipi:service anonymize --enable
$ php artisan cipi:generate-token anonymize
$ php artisan cipi:init-anonymize --scan        # proposes a config from your schema
$ php artisan cipi:anonymize-audit              # config vs live database
```

`--scan` proposes a transformation for every column that looks like personal data (e-mails, names, phones, addresses, IPs, tokens, passwords, tax ids, card data, free text) and empties operational tables (`sessions`, `jobs`, `failed_jobs`, `password_reset_tokens`, `personal_access_tokens`, Telescope, Pulse). Foreign keys and timestamps are never touched. The file is written to `~/.db/anonymization.json` with mode `0640` and is never deployed.

The audit fails on unknown tables, columns or transformations, warns about password columns not set to `password`, and lists uncovered columns that look personal, with a suggestion. **Run it after every migration.**

## Configuration 

Lookup order: `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_CONFIG`, then `~/.db/anonymization.json`, then `~/.cipi/anonymization.json`.

```json
{
  "transformations": {
    "users": {
      "name": "fakeName",
      "email": { "type": "fakeEmail", "unique": true, "consistent": true },
      "password": "password",
      "remember_token": "null",
      "phone": "mask:3,2"
    },
    "orders": {
      "customer_email": { "type": "fakeEmail", "consistent": true },
      "card_last_four": "numerify:####",
      "internal_notes": "fakeParagraph"
    }
  },
  "truncate": ["sessions", "jobs", "failed_jobs", "password_reset_tokens"],
  "options": { "faker_locale": "en_US", "consistent": true, "seed": "change-me" }
}
```

Keys under `transformations` are tables, nested keys are columns. **Columns not listed are copied unchanged**, which is how ids, enums and business fields survive. `NULL` stays `NULL` (except with `fixed`).

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `consistent` | Same original, same fake value, across tables and runs with the same `seed`: `users.email` still joins `orders.customer_email` |
| `unique` | No duplicates in the column; default for `fakeEmail`, `fakeSafeEmail`, `fakeUserName`, `fakeUuid`, `fakeToken`, `fakeIban` |
| `truncate` | Keeps the table, drops its rows |
| `password` | Every row gets the hash of `options.password` (computed once), so developers can log in |

### Transformations 

`php artisan cipi:anonymize --transformations` prints the catalogue.

| Transformation | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `fakeName`, `fakeFirstName`, `fakeLastName`, `fakeUserName` | Names |
| `fakeEmail`, `fakeSafeEmail` | E-mail (`fakeSafeEmail` uses example.com) |
| `fakeCompany`, `fakeJobTitle` | Company, job title |
| `fakeAddress`, `fakeStreetAddress`, `fakeCity`, `fakeState`, `fakePostcode`, `fakeCountry`, `fakeCountryCode` | Postal data |
| `fakePhoneNumber` | Phone |
| `fakeDate`, `fakeDateTime` | `Y-m-d`, `Y-m-d H:i:s` |
| `fakeUrl`, `fakeDomain` | URL, domain |
| `fakeParagraph`, `fakeSentence`, `fakeText[:len]`, `fakeWord` | Free text |
| `fakeIban[:CC]`, `fakeCreditCardNumber` | Banking data in test ranges |
| `fakeIpv4`, `fakeIpv6`, `fakeMacAddress`, `fakeUserAgent` | Network identifiers |
| `fakeUuid`, `fakeToken[:len]`, `fakeIdentifier` | UUID, hex token, tax-id-like value |
| `fakeLatitude`, `fakeLongitude`, `fakeNumber[:digits]`, `fakeBoolean` | Numbers |
| `numerify:###`, `lexify:???`, `bothify:?#` | Patterns (`#` digit, `?` letter) |
| `password` | Hash of `options.password` |
| `null`, `empty`, `fixed:value`, `redact` | `NULL`, `''`, a constant, `[REDACTED]` |
| `hash[:len]`, `mask:first,last`, `keep` | Seeded SHA-256, partial mask (`j*******om`), unchanged |

### Options 

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hash_algorithm` | `auto` | App Hash driver, or `bcrypt`, `argon2id`, `argon2i`, `argon2d` |
| `password` | `password` | Plaintext behind every `password` column |
| `faker_locale` | `en_US` | e.g. `it_IT`, `de_DE` |
| `consistent` | `false` | Default for all columns |
| `seed` | `null` | Keep it private; change it for a different dataset |
| `gzip` | `false` | `.sql.gz` output |
| `connection` | `null` | Another `config/database.php` connection |
| `dump_args` | `[]` | Extra dump flags, one per entry |

> [!warning] Anonymization is **opt-in per column**. PII in a JSON column, a blob or a column you forgot is copied verbatim. Watch `metadata`, `settings` and audit tables.

## Delivery by e-mail 

The API never returns the download URL: **the e-mail is the only channel**, and it goes only to the `email` in the request (no CC, no fallback). Success sends a signed link valid for `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TTL` minutes (default 15); failure sends the error and the job id.

It uses your app's Laravel mail (`MAIL_*`), not the server's `cipi smtp`. Test it before the first export:

```bash
$ php artisan tinker --execute="Mail::raw('test', fn (\$m) => \$m->to('you@example.com')->subject('Mail test'));"
```

> [!warning] `{"status":"queued"}` only means the job was queued. If nothing arrives, check `storage/logs/laravel.log` and `php artisan queue:failed`. The file may already be in `storage/cipi/`.

## HTTP API 

| Method | Endpoint | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/cipi/db` | Bearer token | Validate the config, queue a job (`{"email", "gzip"}`) |
| `POST` | `/cipi/db/user` | Bearer token | Find `users.id` from a production e-mail (ids survive anonymization) |
| `GET` | `/cipi/db/{token}` | Signed URL | Download; expires after the TTL |

```bash
$ curl -sS -X POST "$APP_URL/cipi/db" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TOKEN" \
    -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "developer@example.com"}'
{"status":"queued","email":"developer@example.com","link_valid_minutes":15}

$ curl -sS -L -o anonymized.sql ""
```

| HTTP | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 403 | Bad or missing token | `cipi:generate-token anonymize` |
| 404 | Service disabled or no config | `cipi:service anonymize --enable`, `cipi:init-anonymize` |
| 400 | Invalid `anonymization.json` (all errors listed) | Fix it; `cipi:anonymize-audit` prints the same list |
| 422 | Missing `email` | Send `{"email": "…"}` |
| 410 | Download link expired | Request a new dump |
| 500 | DB error or dump tool missing | Laravel logs, `CIPI_MYSQLDUMP` / `CIPI_PG_DUMP` |

## From your laptop 

`cipi-cli` drives the same flow through the [Cipi API](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client): you name the app, it reads `APP_URL`, `CIPI_ROUTE_PREFIX` and the anonymizer token from the app's `.env`, and calls the agent. No SSH, no token in your shell history.

```bash
$ cipi-cli prod db anonymize myapp --email dev@example.com
→ Requesting anonymized dump of 'myapp' via https://myapp.example.com/cipi/db
✓ Anonymization job queued for 'myapp'

$ cipi-cli db anonymize download "" -o myapp.sql
✓ Saved myapp.sql (24.5 MB)

$ cipi-cli db anonymize download "" -o - | mysql -u root myapp_local
```

Every failure names its fix (service disabled, token missing, custom or Node app, redirect to another host: pass `--url`). The API token needs `apps-view` and `apps-env`, plus `apps-artisan` for remote setup.

## On the server, without HTTP 

```bash
$ php artisan cipi:anonymize                    # → storage/cipi/anonymized_.sql
$ php artisan cipi:anonymize --gzip
$ php artisan cipi:anonymize  
$ php artisan cipi:anonymize --check            # validate + audit, no dump
```

Writes the file directly (no e-mail), reports rows transformed per table, tables emptied and warnings, and exits non-zero on failure. Good for cron and scripts.

## Security checklist 

- Keep `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TOKEN` in a secrets manager; rotate it after team changes; disable the service when unused.
- Tell recipients the shared password, and never use a real one in `options.password`.
- Use `consistent: true` with a private `seed`.
- Run `cipi:anonymize-audit` after every migration.
- Any API token with `apps-env` can read the anonymizer token: scope tokens.
- Verify a dump: grep for a known production e-mail. It must not appear.
- Never commit `anonymization.json`: it maps your schema.


## Agent security & ENV

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/agent-config

Each feature of the agent has **its own token** and can be switched off independently. A disabled route answers 404: hidden, not just forbidden.

| Feature | Token | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Webhook deploy | `CIPI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` | `POST /cipi/webhook` |
| Health | `CIPI_HEALTH_TOKEN` (falls back to the webhook token) | `GET /cipi/health` |
| MCP | `CIPI_MCP_TOKEN` | `POST /cipi/mcp` |
| Anonymizer | `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TOKEN` | `POST /cipi/db`, `/cipi/db/user` |
| Panel tools | `CIPI_TOKEN` (server API token) | outbound, via `cipi/sdk` |

| Area | Protection |
| --- | --- |
| Webhooks | HMAC signatures (GitHub, Bitbucket, Gitea) or token header (GitLab, Azure), constant-time comparisons; what the push claims is recorded as a claim, never as a fact |
| MCP | Command and SQL blocklists, one statement per call, row caps, optional read-only DB, secret redaction, Origin check, no sessions |
| Anonymizer | Config outside the repository (`0640`); DB passwords via environment, never on a command line; raw dump deleted right after; outputs `0600`; signed, expiring download links |

Source: [github.com/cipi-sh/agent](https://github.com/cipi-sh/agent) (MIT).

## Environment variables 

Written by `cipi app create`; toggle features with `php artisan cipi:service  --enable|--disable`.

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CIPI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` | Webhook secret | generated |
| `CIPI_APP_USER` | The app's Linux user | set by Cipi |
| `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH` | Branch that deploys (empty = any) | the app's branch |
| `CIPI_ENV` | Environment label; picks `cipi-.yml` | `production` |
| `CIPI_HOME`, `CIPI_DEPLOY_SCRIPT` | Paths overrides | `/home/`, `~/.deployer/deploy.php` |
| `CIPI_PHP_VERSION` | Reported PHP; used by `cipi:yml generate` | system PHP |
| `CIPI_ROUTE_PREFIX` | Prefix of all agent routes | `cipi` |
| `CIPI_LOG_CHANNEL` | Log channel for deploy events | none |
| `CIPI_HEALTH_CHECK`, `CIPI_HEALTH_TOKEN` | Health endpoint | on, none |
| `CIPI_MCP`, `CIPI_MCP_TOKEN` | MCP endpoint | off, none |
| `CIPI_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Extra browser origins | the app host |
| `CIPI_MCP_DB_WRITE` | Allow writes in `db_query` | `true` |
| `CIPI_MCP_MAX_ROWS` | Row cap (max 500) | 100 |
| `CIPI_MCP_REDACT` | Mask secrets in output | `true` |
| `CIPI_ANONYMIZER`, `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TOKEN` | Anonymizer endpoint | off, none |
| `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_CONFIG`, `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TTL` | Config path; link validity (minutes) | `~/.db/anonymization.json`, 15 |
| `CIPI_MYSQLDUMP`, `CIPI_PG_DUMP` | Dump binaries | from `PATH` |
| `CIPI_PANEL`, `CIPI_PANEL_APP` | Panel MCP tools; app name on the panel | on, `CIPI_APP_USER` |
| `CIPI_BASE_URL`, `CIPI_TOKEN` | Server API URL and token for `cipi/sdk` | none |

> [!tip] For production, set `CIPI_MCP_DB_WRITE=false` unless you really want your assistant to write data.


## Panel overview

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-overview

Cipi is **CLI-first**, and always will be. The web panel is an **optional** layer for people who prefer a browser: your team, a client, or you on a phone. It's a self-hosted Laravel app that drives one or many Cipi servers through the same [REST API](https://cipi.sh/docs/api) as the CLI client and WHMCS. No proprietary control plane, no SaaS, no extra cost.

Real screens of the panel, in motion. Pick a clip, or let them play. Every screen is in the [tour below](#gui-tour).

> [!tip] **Skip it and nothing changes.** Without the panel Cipi stays a lean CLI: no daemon, no web surface, nothing extra listening. Anything done in the browser can be done in the terminal, and the other way round.

```stack
Browser | panel.example.com
cipi/gui | Laravel app on one Cipi server
Cipi API | api., one per managed server
cipi CLI | does the work, as on SSH
```

## What you can do 

| Area | From the panel |
| --- | --- |
| Apps | Create, edit, suspend, delete Laravel (FPM or Octane), Node (SPA, static, SSR with framework presets) and custom apps; environment label; aliases, www ↔ apex, SSL, basic auth |
| Deploy | Deploy, roll back, unlock; a deploy in progress, whoever started it, with its live log; the hash-chained [deploy audit](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-audit) with durations; a log per deploy |
| `cipi.yml` | The file of the live release, whether it's valid, what applying would change, apply as a job, toggle auto-apply |
| Routing | Whole-app and path redirects, prefix reverse proxies |
| App tooling | `.env` editor with masked secrets, Composer `auth.json`, Artisan, allowlisted app commands, saved one-click commands |
| Databases | MariaDB or PostgreSQL per app; create, link to apps, back up, restore (also by uploading a `.sql`/`.sql.gz` from your computer, chunked), rotate passwords |
| Backups | A matrix of apps and databases against [backup profiles](https://cipi.sh/docs/backups): schedule, destination, retention, last run; run now, verify, test destinations |
| Server | Status, CPU, memory, disk, services, PHP versions, Node runtimes, SSH keys, SMTP, health checks, IP allowlist, [disk usage](https://cipi.sh/docs/disk), monitor, Zero Trust status |
| Logs and jobs | App and server logs with filters and live refresh; async jobs in an overlay with colour-coded output; one-time credentials with copy buttons |
| Fleet | Many servers under one login, all apps and databases in one list with a server filter |
| Team | Admins and users; per-server View/Manage and per-app View, Deploy, Edit, Environment, Logs, Commands, Delete; invite links (nothing is e-mailed) |
| Sign-in | Password with optional TOTP, or [single sign-on](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-sso) over OpenID Connect |

Light and dark themes, a phone layout, a time zone per account. A server with an older API or a narrower token keeps working for everything it supports.

> [!security] Permissions are checked on every request, server-side, against the app, server and job the page works on. Installing software, monitor thresholds and Zero Trust changes stay on the CLI by design.

## Screenshot tour 

Real screenshots of the panel against its demo environment: three fictional servers, documentation-range domains and IPs (`./dev/demo.sh` in the package).

### Apps

Every app of every server in one list, with server and type filters, search and a deploy button per row.

Creating an app starts with its type. Node presets (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix, Vite) fill the same defaults as `cipi app create --node`.

### App detail

A header with status, type, runtime and actions, then one tab per area. Tabs live in the URL (`?tab=deploy`), so they can be bookmarked.

### Jobs

Deploys, SSL and database operations run as async jobs. The overlay polls `GET /api/jobs/{id}`, shows elapsed time and colour-codes the output; closing it leaves the job running.

### Databases and server

### Connections and security

### Team and roles

Admins see and do everything. A user gets what an admin grants and is invited with a copyable link that works once and expires after seven days.


## Install the panel

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-install

## Requirements 

The panel talks to servers **only through the Cipi API**. Before installing it:

| You need | Details |
| --- | --- |
| A Cipi server to host it | One of the servers you manage, or a small dedicated box |
| A hostname of its own | e.g. `panel.example.com`, with an `A`/`AAAA` record pointing at that server. It can't share a hostname with an app or with the API (`api.example.com`); Cipi refuses a taken domain |
| `cipi api` on every managed server | With a full-access token, see [API setup](https://cipi.sh/docs/api) |

```bash
$ cipi api token create --name=gui --full-access   # every ability, including future ones
```

PHP, the FPM pool, the Nginx vhost and the scheduler are provisioned by the installer: no Laravel setup by hand.

## Install: `cipi gui ` 

```bash
$ cipi gui panel.example.com
```

```flow
DNS check | domain must point here
Provision | FPM pool, vhost, cron
First admin | e-mail + password
Certificate | Let's Encrypt, HTTPS on
```

The app is bundled at `/opt/cipi/gui`; settings go to `/etc/cipi/gui.json`. The admin password needs **12+ characters** with upper and lower case, a digit and a symbol, and no more than 4 identical characters in a row.

| Flag | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| `--skip-dns-check` | Behind a NAT or proxy the check can't see through |
| `--no-ssl` | You'll issue the certificate later with `cipi gui ssl` |

## SSL: `cipi gui ssl` 

Issues (or re-issues) the Let's Encrypt certificate and switches the panel to HTTPS, for a certificate skipped with `--no-ssl` or one that failed. It checks DNS first, exits 1 if certbot fails, and renews with the same automation as app domains.

```bash
$ cipi gui ssl
```

## Change domain: `cipi gui move` 

```bash
$ cipi gui move panel.newdomain.com           # move and issue the new certificate
$ cipi gui move panel.newdomain.com --no-ssl  # certificate later
```

| What happens | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Kept | Accounts, 2FA enrolments, server connections (admins sign in again) |
| Vhost | Rewritten; if `nginx -t` rejects it, the old one comes back and nothing changes |
| Config | `/etc/cipi/gui.json` and `APP_URL` updated |
| SSL | Old certificate deleted, new one issued; on failure the panel stays on HTTP until `cipi gui ssl` |

Managed servers need no change: the panel calls their API URLs, and their allowlists are by IP. To move a server's API, use [`cipi api move`](https://cipi.sh/docs/api) there and update its URL under Connections.

> [!info] With [Cloudflare Zero Trust](https://cipi.sh/docs/zero-trust): run `cipi zt hostname remove --gui` before the move, then `cipi zt hostname add --gui` and `cipi zt access enable --gui`. The move refuses to run while the hostname is on the tunnel.

## Two-factor authentication 

Session login with **optional TOTP** per user (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Aegis…), enrolled from the profile. With [single sign-on](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-sso), MFA is the identity provider's job and the TOTP step is skipped for SSO sign-ins.

Lost a second factor? From the server, [`cipi gui reset-user`](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-maintenance) rewrites the account and removes the enrolment.


## Single sign-on

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-sso

The panel can sign people in through your identity provider over **OpenID Connect**: Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel, Auth0, anything with a `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. SAML isn't supported. SSO is opt-in and configured **from the server**, which is also the break-glass if a provider breaks.

```flow
Register | OIDC client at your IdP
cipi gui sso set | issuer, client id, secret
Sign in | button on the login page
Match | by e-mail, then by identity
```

## 1. Register the panel at your provider 

Create an OIDC web client with redirect URI `https:///auth/sso/callback`. Keep the client id, secret and issuer URL.

| Provider | Where | Issuer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft Entra ID | App registrations → New (single-tenant, Web) → Certificates & secrets | `https://login.microsoftonline.com//v2.0`, never `common` or `organizations` |
| Google Workspace | Cloud console → Credentials → OAuth client ID (Web) | `https://accounts.google.com`; restrict with `--domains` |
| Okta, Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel, Auth0 | Standard OIDC web client, authorization-code flow | The realm or app URL whose discovery document answers |

## 2. Turn it on 

```bash
$ cipi gui sso set --issuer=https://login.microsoftonline.com//v2.0 \
    --client-id= --client-secret=     # secret is asked if omitted
$ cipi gui sso set --issuer=https://accounts.google.com --client-id=… --domains=example.com
$ cipi gui sso status          # issuer, label, redirect URI, who can get in
$ cipi gui sso only on         # SSO button only, passwords off
$ cipi gui sso only off        # break-glass: passwords back
$ cipi gui sso disable         # back to passwords; links are kept
```

`set` writes the panel's `.env`, clears the config cache, runs the migration and prints the **redirect URI** to check against the provider.

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--issuer=` | Required, `https://` only; discovery cached for an hour |
| `--client-id=` | Required |
| `--client-secret=` | Asked when omitted; kept when you re-run `set` |
| `--label=` | Button text (default from the issuer: Microsoft Entra ID, Google, Okta, SSO) |
| `--domains=a.com,b.com` | People from these domains get an account on first sign-in (role user, no access until granted) |
| `--only` | Same as `sso only on` |
| `--scopes=` | Instead of `openid email profile` |

## 3. Who gets in 

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing account | Matched by e-mail (case-insensitive) on first sign-in, then linked to the identity: a renamed mailbox still lands on the same account |
| E-mail linked to another identity | Refused |
| New person, domain in `--domains` | Account created as a user with no grants |
| Anyone else | "No panel account… ask an admin for an invite link". Nothing is created |

Roles and grants stay the panel's; SSO-linked accounts carry a badge in Team.

> [!security] Authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256), `state` and `nonce`; code exchanged server-to-server; identity read from the userinfo endpoint; issuer, audience and nonce checked. `email_verified: false` is refused. Every change is logged in `cipi.log` and raises the `gui_sso` notification.

## 4. Troubleshooting 

| Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Locked out with SSO-only | `cipi gui sso only off`, or `cipi gui sso disable`, or [`cipi gui reset-user`](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-maintenance). Nothing in the panel can bypass SSO-only |
| `redirect_uri mismatch` | Register exactly what `sso status` prints; after [`cipi gui move`](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-install) register the new one |
| `issuer mismatch` | Use the exact `issuer` from the discovery document (Entra: tenant id, not `common`) |
| `no email claim` | Give the account a mail address and grant `openid`, `email`, `profile` (`preferred_username` isn't accepted) |
| New issuer or client id | Links are forgotten (identities are per provider); everyone relinks by e-mail at next sign-in |


## Update & remove

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-maintenance

## Update 

The panel is the `cipi/gui` Composer package, so updating is Composer plus migrations.

| Command | What it does | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cipi gui update` | `composer update cipi/gui`, migrations, theme refresh | Routine updates |
| `cipi gui upgrade` | Rebuilds the app code from scratch | Major releases, or a drifted install |
| `cipi gui refresh-theme` | Recompiles the theme only | After a theme tweak |

> [!tip] Keep the panel and each server's API current together (`cipi gui update`, `cipi api update`) so forms and lists match what servers offer.

## Operations 

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cipi gui status` | Installed or not, domain, health of its services |
| `cipi gui fix-permissions` | Repairs the FPM `open_basedir` and runtime permissions; run it on permission or autoload errors after an update |
| `cipi gui reset-user` | Rewrites an admin's e-mail, name and password and clears their 2FA (alias `reset-password`) |

Locked out by [SSO-only](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-sso)? `cipi gui sso only off` brings password sign-in back first.

## Remove 

```bash
$ cipi gui remove           # alias: uninstall
$ cipi gui remove --force   # no confirmation
```

Removes the vhost, FPM pool, scheduler, app, config and the panel's certificate (one still used by an app is kept). Servers and apps are untouched: the panel is only an API client. A panel on the Cloudflare tunnel must come off it first (`cipi zt hostname remove --gui`). The API on each server stays; remove it with [`cipi api remove`](https://cipi.sh/docs/api) if nothing else uses it.


## Panel architecture

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/gui-architecture

The panel is a standard **Laravel** application distributed as the `cipi/gui` package ([cipi-sh/gui](https://github.com/cipi-sh/gui)). It holds **no state about your infrastructure**: it authenticates to each server's API, submits jobs and polls them. Tear it down and rebuild it elsewhere without touching a managed server.

| Aspect | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | Laravel 12 or 13, Livewire 3.6+ or 4, no asset build step |
| Package | `cipi/gui` from GitHub, Composer VCS `dev-main` |
| Install path | `/opt/cipi/gui` |
| Config | `/etc/cipi/gui.json` |
| Isolation | Own FPM pool, `open_basedir` limited to its own directories |
| Auth | Session login, optional TOTP, optional OpenID Connect SSO |
| Jobs | No local queue worker: remote jobs polled through each server's API |

```stack
Panel (cipi/gui) | sessions, roles, server connections
HTTPS + Bearer token | one per server, IP allowlist
Cipi API (cipi/api) | queues async jobs
cipi CLI via sudoers | the same code path as SSH
```

## API coverage 

| Area | Endpoints used |
| --- | --- |
| Server | `GET /api/status`; PHP, DB engines, Node runtimes, SSH keys, services, SMTP, search, packages, monitor, Zero Trust, `GET /api/disk` and `/api/disk/dbs`, IP allowlist |
| Apps | CRUD, suspend, fix-permissions, basic auth, logs, `.env`, `auth.json`, Artisan, app commands; create with `engine`, `octane`, Node options; webhook rotation; per-app health check |
| Deploy | Deploy, rollback, unlock, `deploy/audit`, `deploy/history`, `GET /api/deploys/last`, `deploy-config` |
| `cipi.yml` | `GET /api/apps/{name}/yml`, `POST …/yml/apply`, `…/yml/auto/enable|disable` |
| Domains | Aliases, www ↔ apex, SSL install and force HTTPS |
| Routing | `/api/apps/{name}/redirect*`, `/api/apps/{name}/proxies` |
| Node | `GET /api/node`, `/api/apps/{name}/node`, SSR restart |
| Search | `GET /api/search`, per-app enable/disable |
| Databases | List, create, back up, restore (with chunked upload), rotate password, link to apps; deletion stays on the host CLI |
| Backups | `/api/backups…` profiles, runs, destinations test |
| Jobs | Status, output and parsed `result` (credentials, backup file, webhook token) |

A server with an older API keeps every page it supports; a missing tab says what it needs. Disk sizes are measured when the tab opens, with their own timeout (`CIPI_GUI_HTTP_DISK_TIMEOUT`, 180 s). `cipi ssh apps`, `cipi firewall attempts`, disk limits and DNS accounts are changed on the host.

> [!info] Prefer the terminal? The [CLI client](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client) does the same over the API, and the [WHMCS module](https://cipi.sh/docs/whmcs) automates it for hosting providers.


## REST API

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/api

`cipi api ` adds an **optional REST API and MCP server** to a Cipi server. It's what the [web panel](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui), [cipi-cli](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client), the [PHP SDK](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-sdk), [WHMCS](https://cipi.sh/docs/whmcs) and your AI assistant talk to. It's a separate Laravel app ([`cipi/api`](https://github.com/cipi-sh/api), MIT) that runs as `www-data` and calls an **allowlist of `cipi` commands** through sudo: credentials never leave Cipi, and destructive host operations stay on the CLI.

| It exposes | Where |
| --- | --- |
| REST API for apps, deploys, domains, SSL, databases, backups, Node, search, `cipi.yml`, server status | `/api/*` |
| MCP server for AI assistants | `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) |
| Interactive reference (Swagger UI, OpenAPI) | `/docs` |

```stack
Client | panel, cipi-cli, SDK, CI, MCP
HTTPS + Sanctum token | abilities, IP allowlist
cipi/api | sync reads, async jobs (SQLite queue)
sudo allowlist | /etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api
cipi CLI | the same code path as SSH
```

This is **server-level** automation. The per-app [Cipi Agent](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent) (`cipi/agent`) is a different package.

## A domain of its own 

The API has its own vhost and certificate, so it needs a hostname **only it uses**. Point an `A`/`AAAA` record at the server first: the command checks DNS and stops with the record to create (`--skip-dns-check` behind a NAT or proxy it can't see through; the Cloudflare proxy counts as pointing here).

| What | Example | Set up with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your app | `example.com`, `www.example.com` | `cipi app create`, `cipi alias add` |
| API + MCP | `api.example.com` | `cipi api api.example.com` |
| Web panel | `panel.example.com` | `cipi gui panel.example.com` |

All three can share a server and a registered domain; each hostname belongs to one of them. Cipi refuses any overlap, in both directions (`cipi app create`, `alias add`, `app clone`, `sync import` and `cipi.yml` aliases won't take the API's or the panel's hostname). `cipi api status` warns if an old install shares a hostname with an app: fix it with [`cipi api move`](#cipi-api-move).

## Commands 

```bash
$ cipi api api.example.com          # DNS check, install, certificate, first token
$ cipi api ssl                      # (re)issue the certificate
$ cipi api status                   # versions, queue worker, pending jobs, FPM pool
$ cipi api token list
$ cipi api token create --name=panel --full-access
$ cipi api token create --name=ci --abilities=apps-view,deploy-manage --expires=2027-06-30
$ cipi api token revoke 
$ cipi api update                   # soft update (also nightly at 04:30)
$ cipi api upgrade                  # full rebuild, rollback kept at /opt/cipi/api.old
$ cipi api fix-permissions          # storage/database ownership back to www-data
```

Install flags: `--no-ssl`, `--no-token`, `--skip-dns-check`.

## Change domain: `cipi api move` 

```bash
$ cipi api move api.newdomain.com           # move and issue the certificate
$ cipi api move api.newdomain.com --no-ssl  # certificate later with cipi api ssl
```

Tokens, job history and the IP allowlist stay. The vhost is rewritten (and restored if `nginx -t` fails), `/etc/cipi/api.json` and `APP_URL` updated, `cipi-queue` restarted, the old certificate deleted (never one still used by an app) and a new one issued. Then update the URL in every client: panel Connections, cipi-cli profile, SDK config, MCP clients. Running `cipi api ` on a configured server points you here instead of silently moving.

## Remove: `cipi api remove` 

```bash
$ cipi api remove           # alias: uninstall; --force skips the prompt
```

Removes the `cipi-queue` worker, vhost, FPM pool, crons, certificate, `/opt/cipi/api` (and backups), `api.json`, the IP allowlist and logs. **All tokens die with it.** Apps, databases and the panel are untouched; the sudoers allowlist stays because it's part of every Cipi install.

## Tokens and abilities 

Authentication is **Sanctum** Bearer tokens. Each token gets a list of abilities, or `--full-access` (the wildcard `*`, which also covers abilities added in future releases). Give a CI job only what it needs: `deploy-manage` alone deploys.

| Area | Abilities |
| --- | --- |
| Apps | `apps-view`, `apps-create`, `apps-edit`, `apps-delete`, `apps-suspend`, `apps-basicauth` |
| App tooling | `apps-env`, `apps-auth` (Composer `auth.json`), `apps-artisan`, `apps-run`, `apps-deploy-config` |
| Deploy | `deploy-manage` (deploy, rollback, unlock, audit, status) |
| `cipi.yml` | `yml-view`, `yml-manage` |
| Domains and SSL | `aliases-view`, `aliases-create`, `aliases-delete`, `www-manage`, `ssl-manage` |
| Routing | `redirects-view`, `redirects-manage`, `proxies-view`, `proxies-manage` |
| Node | `node-view`, `node-manage` (SSR restart), `node-runtimes-manage` |
| Databases | `dbs-view`, `dbs-create`, `dbs-manage` |
| Backups | `backups-view` (never keys), `backups-manage` |
| Server | `status-view`, `php-view`, `php-manage`, `ssh-view`, `ssh-manage`, `services-view`, `services-manage`, `smtp-view`, `smtp-manage`, `health-view`, `health-manage`, `ip-whitelist-view`, `ip-whitelist-manage` |
| Read-only insights | `search-view`, `search-manage`, `packages-view`, `monitor-view`, `zt-view`, `disk-view` |
| MCP | `mcp-access` (covers every MCP tool) |

`php artisan cipi:token-abilities` (or the `cipi api token create` checklist) shows the canonical list.

## REST endpoints 

Every call needs `Authorization: Bearer `. **Reads are synchronous. Writes are async jobs**: they answer `202` with a `job_id`; poll `GET /api/jobs/{id}` (with the ability the job was created under) for status, output and a structured `result` (credentials, backup path, webhook token).

### Apps 

| Method | Path | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/apps`, `/api/apps/{name}` | `apps-view` |
| `POST` | `/api/apps` | `apps-create` |
| `PUT` | `/api/apps/{name}` | `apps-edit` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/apps/{name}` | `apps-delete` |
| `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/suspend`, `/unsuspend` | `apps-suspend` |
| `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/fix-permissions`, `/webhook/recreate` | `apps-edit` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/basicauth`, `/enable`, `/disable` | `apps-basicauth` |
| `GET`, `PUT` | `/api/apps/{name}/env` | `apps-env` |
| `GET` `POST` `PUT` `DELETE` | `/api/apps/{name}/auth` | `apps-auth` |
| `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/artisan` | `apps-artisan` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/run-commands`, `/api/apps/{name}/run` | `apps-run` |
| `GET`, `PUT` | `/api/apps/{name}/deploy-config` | `apps-deploy-config` |
| `GET`, `PUT` | `/api/apps/{name}/limits` | `apps-view` / `apps-edit` |
| `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE` | `/api/apps/{name}/health`, `POST …/health/check` | `health-view` / `health-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/apps/{name}/logs?type=&page=&per_page=` | `apps-view` |

`POST /api/apps` takes `domain`, `repository`, `branch`, `php`, `env`, `engine` (`mariadb`/`pgsql`), `octane`, `node_build`, `custom` + `docroot` (repository optional for SFTP-only sites), or Node fields (`node`: `spa|static|ssr`, `framework`, `node_version`, `build`, `start`, `output`, `health_path`). The same rules as [`cipi app create`](https://cipi.sh/docs/create-app) apply. `PUT` forwards only fields that changed; a `domain` already used elsewhere answers `409`. App objects return `type` (`laravel`, `custom`, `node`), `env`, `suspended`, `basic_auth`, `octane`, `redirects`, `proxies` and `databases`.

### Deploy and cipi.yml 

| Method | Path | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/deploy`, `/deploy/rollback`, `/deploy/unlock` | `deploy-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/apps/{name}/deploy/status?tail=N` | `deploy-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/apps/{name}/deploy/audit?days=90` | `deploy-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/apps/{name}/deploy/history?limit=N`, `/api/deploys/last` | `apps-view` or `deploy-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/apps/{name}/yml` | `yml-view` |
| `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/yml/apply` (job) | `yml-manage` |
| `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/yml/auto/enable`, `/disable` | `yml-manage` |

`deploy/status` is safe to poll: running, queued, interrupted or idle, with trigger, branch, phase, elapsed time and optional log tail. `deploy/audit` returns the [hash-chained ledger](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-audit).

GET /api/apps/{name}/yml is cipi yml plan &lt;app&gt; --json: the file of the live release, env, auto, valid and errors, in_sync, warnings, changes (kind, token, summary), blockers and notes. See cipi.yml.

### Domains, SSL and routing 

| Method | Path | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` | `/api/apps/{name}/aliases[/{alias}]` | `aliases-*` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/www`, `/add`, `/force-to-root`, `/force-from-root`, `/clear` | `www-manage` |
| `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/ssl` (`dns`, `account`, `wildcard`, `http`), `/ssl/force` | `ssl-manage` |
| `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE` | `/api/ssl/dns[/{account}]` (Cloudflare accounts; token never returned) | `ssl-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/apps/{name}/redirects` | `redirects-view` |
| `PUT`, `DELETE`, `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/redirect`, `/redirect/enable`, `/disable`, `/redirects` | `redirects-manage` |
| `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` | `/api/apps/{name}/proxies` | `proxies-view` / `proxies-manage` |

Redirects and proxies use the CLI's own validation, regenerate the vhost and revert if `nginx -t` fails. The loopback guard on proxies is **never bypassed from the API**.

### Databases and backups 

| Method | Path | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/dbs?engine=`, `/api/dbs/engines` | `dbs-view` |
| `POST` | `/api/dbs` (`name`, `engine`, `app`) | `dbs-create` |
| `POST` | `/api/dbs/{name}/backup`, `/restore`, `/password` | `dbs-manage` |
| `POST`, `DELETE` | `/api/dbs/{name}/link` | `dbs-manage` |
| `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` | `/api/dbs/uploads/limits`, `/api/dbs/uploads`, `/uploads/{id}/chunks` | `dbs-manage` |
| `POST` | `/api/dbs/engines/install` | `dbs-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/backups`, `/api/backups/runs` | `backups-view` |
| `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` | `/api/backups/run`, `/verify`, `/destinations/test`, `/profiles[/{name}]`, `…/enable`, `…/disable` | `backups-manage` |

Restore takes a server `file` or an `upload_id`: dumps (`.sql`, `.sql.gz`, up to 2 GB by default) are uploaded in chunks and deleted when the job ends. **Backup destinations are read-only** over the API: S3 secret keys are added on the server with `cipi backup destination add`.

### Server 

| Method | Path | Ability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/status` (same JSON as `cipi status`) | `status-view` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/php`, `/api/php/install` | `php-view` / `php-manage` |
| `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` | `/api/ssh/keys[/{n}]` | `ssh-view` / `ssh-manage` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/services`, `/services/{name}/restart` | `services-view` / `services-manage` |
| `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `POST` | `/api/smtp`, `/smtp/enable`, `/disable`, `/test` | `smtp-view` / `smtp-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/health` | `health-view` |
| `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` | `/api/node`, `/node/install`, `/node/upgrade`, `/node/default`, `/node/{major}` | `node-view` / `node-runtimes-manage` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/apps/{name}/node`, `/node/restart` (blue/green) | `node-view` / `node-manage` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/search`, `/api/apps/{name}/search/enable`, `/disable` | `search-view` / `search-manage` |
| `GET` | `/api/disk`, `/api/disk/dbs` | `disk-view` |
| `GET` | `/api/packages`, `/api/monitor`, `/api/zt` | `packages-view`, `monitor-view`, `zt-view` |
| `GET` | `/api/jobs/{id}` | the job's ability |

> [!security] **Kept off the API on purpose:** removing PHP versions, switching default PHP or engine, dropping databases, installing Meilisearch or host packages, stack upgrades, monitor thresholds and every Zero Trust change. Installing software or destroying data is an operator decision taken at the CLI, so a compromised token can't do it.

## Examples 

```bash
$ export CIPI_API_URL=https://api.example.com CIPI_API_TOKEN=
$ H="Authorization: Bearer $CIPI_API_TOKEN"

$ curl -sS "$CIPI_API_URL/api/apps" -H "$H" -H "Accept: application/json"

$ curl -sS -X POST "$CIPI_API_URL/api/apps" -H "$H" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"domain":"shop.example.com","repository":"git@github.com:you/shop.git","branch":"main","octane":true,"engine":"mariadb"}'
{"job_id":"9f1c…","status":"pending"}

$ curl -sS -X POST "$CIPI_API_URL/api/apps/shop/deploy" -H "$H"
$ curl -sS "$CIPI_API_URL/api/jobs/9f1c…" -H "$H"      # poll until completed

$ curl -sS -X PUT "$CIPI_API_URL/api/apps/shop/env" -H "$H" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"set":{"APP_DEBUG":"false"},"unset":["LEGACY_KEY"]}'

$ curl -sS -X POST "$CIPI_API_URL/api/apps/shop/artisan" -H "$H" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"command":"cache:clear"}'

$ curl -sS -X POST "$CIPI_API_URL/api/apps/shop/proxies" -H "$H" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"prefix":"/api/","upstream":"http://127.0.0.1:3000","strip_prefix":true}'
```

A database backup through the API is a **real** backup. For a dump people can share, use the [anonymizer](https://cipi.sh/docs/anonymizer).

## Host integration 

The API runs as `www-data` and calls `cipi` through `/etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api`, an explicit allowlist of subcommands with their exact argument shapes, checked with `visudo -cf` whenever a migration regenerates it. Vault and MariaDB credentials stay inside Cipi, never in PHP. Its FPM pool has its own `open_basedir`.

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP 500 on `/docs` or `/mcp` after an update | `cipi api fix-permissions`, then `cipi api status` |
| `sudo: a terminal is required` | `cipi self-update` regenerates the allowlist |
| Panel says backups aren't configured | Compare `ls -l /etc/cipi/backup.json` with `sudo -u www-data sudo -n /usr/local/bin/cipi backup status --json` |

## IP allowlist 

Restrict REST and MCP clients by source IP. `/etc/cipi/api-ip-whitelist` holds one IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR per line; `*` or no file allows all. Rejected clients get `403 {"error":"IP not allowed","ip":"…"}`.

```bash
$ cipi api ip-whitelist show [--json]
$ cipi api ip-whitelist add 203.0.113.10
$ cipi api ip-whitelist set --ips=203.0.113.0/24,2001:db8::/32
$ cipi api ip-whitelist allow-all
```

Over REST (`/api/ip-whitelist`), `PUT` adds the caller's IP when tightening the list unless `ensure_client_ip: false`, so you can't lock yourself out by accident. The file is replaced atomically.

## MCP server 

`/mcp` exposes the server to AI assistants: apps, deploys and audit, domains, SSL, redirects, proxies, Node, databases, search, limits, disk, `cipi.yml`, server management, logs, Artisan and job polling. A token with `mcp-access` covers every tool. Async tools return a `job_id` to poll with `JobShow`; log tools prepend a production warning and redact secrets.

```bash
$ claude mcp add --transport http cipi-api https://api.example.com/mcp \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer "
```

Setup for Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop and others is in [MCP servers](https://cipi.sh/docs/mcp).

## The `cipi/api` package 

`cipi api ` provisions everything (`/opt/cipi/api`, Nginx, SSL, SQLite job queue, `cipi-queue.service`). For custom setups:

```bash
$ composer require cipi/api
$ php artisan vendor:publish --tag=cipi-config
$ php artisan vendor:publish --tag=cipi-assets
$ php artisan migrate
$ php artisan cipi:seed-api-user
$ php artisan cipi:token-create
```

Requires PHP 8.3+ and Laravel 12.41+ or 13. The panel reads `CIPI_APPS_JSON=/etc/cipi/apps.json` (or the `apps-public.json` projection). Abilities live in `config/cipi.php`.


## CLI client (cipi-cli)

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client

`cipi-cli` manages your Cipi servers **from your laptop, without SSH**. It's a single Go binary (Linux and macOS, amd64 and arm64, MIT) that talks to each server's [Cipi API](https://cipi.sh/docs/api): apps, deploys, `cipi.yml`, SSL, databases and anonymized dumps, PHP, services, keys, SMTP, health checks and disk usage. One profile per server, so a fleet is one command away.

> [!info] Each server needs [`cipi api`](https://cipi.sh/docs/api) installed, and a token from `cipi api token create`.

## Install 

```bash
$ chmod +x cipi-cli-* && sudo mv cipi-cli-* /usr/local/bin/cipi-cli   # from GitHub Releases
$ cipi-cli version
```

Binaries ship with SHA-256 checksums on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/cipi-sh/cli/releases). From source: `git clone https://github.com/cipi-sh/cli && cd cli && make build && sudo make install`.

## Configure a server 

A **profile** is one server: API endpoint plus token, stored in `~/.cipi/config.json` (mode `0600`).

```bash
$ cipi-cli api token add prod
Cipi API endpoint: https://api.example.com
API token: 1|yourtoken...
Server profile "prod" saved → ~/.cipi/config.json

$ cipi-cli profiles add staging --endpoint https://api.staging.example.com --token "1|…"
```

## Profiles 

Prefix any command with a profile to target that server, or set a default.

```bash
$ cipi-cli prod deploy shop
$ cipi-cli profiles use prod
$ cipi-cli apps list               # uses prod
$ cipi-cli staging apps list       # an explicit prefix still wins
```

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `profiles` / `profiles list` | List servers (alias `servers`) |
| `profiles add ` | Add or update (`--endpoint`, `--token`) |
| `profiles show [name]` | One profile, token masked, or all |
| `profiles use ` | Default server |
| `profiles delete ` | Local credentials only; nothing changes on the server |

## `apps` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `apps list`, `apps show ` | List, details (environment included) |
| `apps create [flags]` | Create; prints credentials, deploy key and whether the key can read the repository |
| `apps edit  [flags]` | PHP, repository, branch, environment, domain, Node settings |
| `apps delete  [-y]` | Delete |
| `apps suspend`, `unsuspend ` | 503 maintenance page, without deleting |
| `apps logs  [--type --page --per-page]` | nginx, php, laravel, worker, deploy; page 1 is newest |
| `apps artisan  ` | Artisan as an async job |
| `apps run  ` | Allowlisted binaries (`cipi-cli run-commands`) |
| `apps env show|set ` | Read `.env`, or `--set KEY=VALUE` / `--unset KEY` |
| `apps auth show|create|update|delete ` | Composer `auth.json` |
| `apps basicauth status|enable|disable ` | HTTP Basic Auth |
| `apps node status|restart ` | Node status, blue/green restart |
| `apps search enable|disable ` | Meilisearch for one app |
| `apps webhook recreate  [--rotate-secret]` | New Git webhook, optionally a new secret |
| `apps fix-permissions ` | Restore home permissions |

| Create flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--user`, `--domain` | App name (Linux user, database), primary domain |
| `--repository`, `--branch` | Git source |
| `--php` | e.g. `8.6` |
| `--env` | Environment label; picks [`cipi-.yml`](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml) |
| `--engine` | `mariadb` or `pgsql` |
| `--octane` | `true` / `frankenphp` |
| `--node-build` | Asset build on every deploy, e.g. `npm ci && npm run build` |
| `--custom`, `--docroot` | Non-Laravel app |
| `--node`, `--framework`, `--node-version`, `--build`, `--start`, `--output`, `--health-path` | [Node apps](https://cipi.sh/docs/node-apps) |

```bash
$ cipi-cli apps create --user=shop --domain=shop.com --php=8.6 \
    --repository=git@github.com:acme/shop.git --branch=main --node-build='npm ci && npm run build'
$ cipi-cli apps create --user=shop-stg --domain=staging.shop.com \
    --repository=git@github.com:acme/shop.git --branch=develop --env=staging
$ cipi-cli apps create --user=web --domain=web.acme.com --node=ssr --framework=next \
    --repository=git@github.com:acme/web.git
$ cipi-cli apps artisan shop migrate --force
$ cipi-cli apps env set shop --set APP_DEBUG=false --unset OLD_KEY
$ cipi-cli apps logs shop --type=deploy
```

Subcommands need the matching token abilities (`apps-artisan`, `apps-run`, `apps-env`, `apps-auth`).

## `domains` 

Every primary domain and alias on the server in one table: handy to audit DNS or spot missing certificates.

```bash
$ cipi-cli domains
 DOMAIN          APP    KIND     TYPE     PHP  SSL
 shop.com        shop   primary  Laravel  8.6  ✓
 www.shop.com    shop   alias    Laravel  8.6  ✓
```

## `deploy` and `yml` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy ` | Zero-downtime deploy, waits for the job |
| `deploy rollback  [-y]` | Previous release |
| `deploy unlock ` | Clear a stuck lock |
| `deploy config show|set ` | `deploy.php` options: `--optimize`, `--storage-link`, `--queue-restart`, `--horizon-terminate`, `--predeploy-snapshot`, `--node-build`, `--extra-artisan` |
| `deploy audit  [--days N]` | [Deploy ledger](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-audit): origin, operator, IP, commit |
| `yml ` | The live `cipi.yml`: file, environment, validity, what applying would change |
| `yml apply ` | Apply it as a job |
| `yml auto  on|off|status` | Apply after every deploy (asks for confirmation) |

```bash
$ cipi-cli deploy shop
Deploying shop...
Polling job #42... completed
Deployed to release #14. Zero downtime.
```

`yml` needs a token with `yml-view` / `yml-manage`. With auto-apply on, anyone who can push can change the app's server settings: that's the point, and the reason it asks first.

## `ssl` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `ssl install ` | Let's Encrypt for the primary domain and all aliases |
| `ssl force ` | Re-apply the HTTP → HTTPS redirect |

## `www` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `www status ` | Current www / apex setup |
| `www add ` | Add the counterpart as an alias |
| `www force-to-root` / `force-from-root ` | 301 to apex / to www |
| `www clear ` | Remove the canonical redirect |

## `redirect` and `proxies` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `redirect list ` | Whole-app and path redirects |
| `redirect set  --to URL [--code] [--keep-path]` | Whole app to a URL, one hop |
| `redirect enable|disable|unset ` | Toggle or remove it |
| `redirect add  --from /path --to URL` | Path redirect; a trailing `/` means prefix |
| `redirect remove  --from /path` | Remove |
| `proxies list|add|remove ` | Prefix proxies (`--prefix`, `--upstream`, `--strip-prefix`, `--preserve-host`, `--timeout`, `--buffering`) |

```bash
$ cipi-cli redirect add shop --from /blog/ --to https://blog.acme.com/
$ cipi-cli proxies add shop --prefix /api --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8080 --strip-prefix
```

## `aliases` 

```bash
$ cipi-cli aliases add shop www.shop.com
$ cipi-cli aliases list shop
$ cipi-cli aliases remove shop old.shop.com -y
$ cipi-cli ssl install shop      # re-issue to cover new aliases
```

## `db` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `db engines`, `db install ` | Installed engines; install `mariadb` or `pgsql` |
| `db list [--engine]` | Databases with sizes |
| `db create  [--engine]` | Create |
| `db backup ` | Compressed backup on the server |
| `db restore  [-y]` | Restore the latest backup |
| `db password ` | New password, linked app `.env` updated |
| `db anonymize  --email` | Anonymized dump through `cipi/agent` |
| `db anonymize download  [-o file]` | Download from the signed link (`-o -` for stdout) |

Anonymized dumps

The CLI reads `APP_URL` and the anonymizer token from the app's `.env` through the API and calls the [agent](https://cipi.sh/docs/anonymizer) on the app. The signed link arrives by e-mail and lasts 15 minutes.

```bash
$ cipi-cli apps artisan shop cipi:service anonymize --enable
$ cipi-cli apps artisan shop cipi:generate-token anonymize
$ cipi-cli apps artisan shop cipi:init-anonymize
$ cipi-cli prod db anonymize shop --email dev@example.com
✓ Anonymization job queued for 'shop'
$ cipi-cli db anonymize download "" -o - | mysql -u root shop_local
```

Flags: `--email`, `--url` (when the app redirects, redirects are never followed), `--token`, `-o`, `--force`. Custom and Node apps are refused.

## `php` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `php list` | Installed versions, FPM status, default; legacy versions marked |
| `php install ` | `8.3`, `8.4`, `8.5` or `8.6` (async job) |

Switching the default and removing versions stay on the server (`cipi php switch|remove`).

## `services` and `ssh-keys` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `services list [name]` | Status of system services |
| `services restart ` | e.g. `nginx`, `mariadb`, `php8.6-fpm` |
| `ssh-keys list` | Authorized keys of the `cipi` user, with ids |
| `ssh-keys add [key] [--file F]` | Add a public key |
| `ssh-keys remove ` | Remove one |

## `smtp` 

Server notification e-mail. The stored password is never shown.

```bash
$ cipi-cli smtp set --host smtp.example.com --port 587 --user notify@example.com \
    --password "s3cret" --from notify@example.com --to ops@example.com
$ cipi-cli smtp test
```

Also `smtp show`, `smtp enable|disable`, `smtp delete`. Omitted flags keep stored values; `--no-test` skips the test e-mail.

## `health` 

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `health list`, `health show ` | Checks and last result |
| `health set  [--url] [--expect]` | Enable (default `https:///up`, expect `200`) |
| `health unset ` | Disable |
| `health check ` | Run now; **exits 1 when unhealthy**, a ready-made CI gate |

## `ip-whitelist` 

```bash
$ cipi-cli ip-whitelist set 203.0.113.10 198.51.100.0/24
$ cipi-cli ip-whitelist add|remove 
$ cipi-cli ip-whitelist allow-all
```

Your current IP is kept when tightening the list (`--no-ensure-client-ip` to skip).

## Server insights 

Read-only, `--json` everywhere: `search status`, `node list`, `monitor`, `packages`, `zt` (Zero Trust), `run-commands`.

## `status` 

```bash
$ cipi-cli status
 NAME      IP             CPU   RAM          HDD          APPS  SVC     CIPI
 prod*     203.0.113.10   12%   48% (3840M)  42G/80G 53%  3     8/8 ok  5.10.0
 staging   203.0.113.20    4%   31% (2048M)  18G/40G 45%  1     8/8 ok  5.10.0

$ cipi-cli status prod      # full detail for one server
```

## `disk` 

```bash
$ cipi-cli disk
 APP    FILES    DATABASE  TOTAL    DISK  LIMIT
 shop   2.00 GB  1.00 GB   3.00 GB  3.0%  10 GB (30%)
 blog   0.50 GB  120.4 MB  0.62 GB  0.6%  —
$ cipi-cli disk db          # every database, in MB
```

Same figures as [`cipi disk`](https://cipi.sh/docs/disk). Sizes are measured on request (up to three minutes). LIMIT is the soft limit from [`cipi app limits`](https://cipi.sh/docs/limits): alerts only.

## `jobs` 

`jobs show ` and `jobs wait ` (blocking). Write commands wait for their job by default.

## `update` 

```bash
$ cipi-cli update          # highest release, checksum verified (aliases self-update, upgrade)
$ cipi-cli update --force  # reinstall, allows downgrade
```

## `completion` 

```bash
$ cipi-cli completion install                # detects zsh, bash or fish
$ cipi-cli completion install --shell bash
```

## Global flags 

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output for scripts and CI |
| `--no-color` | Plain output |
| `--help` | Help for any command |

```bash
$ cipi-cli apps list --json | jq '.[].name'
```

## Token abilities by command 

| Commands | Abilities |
| --- | --- |
| `apps list/show`, `domains`, `apps logs` | `apps-view` |
| `apps create/edit/delete/suspend` | `apps-create`, `apps-edit`, `apps-delete`, `apps-suspend` |
| `apps env/auth/artisan/run`, `deploy config` | `apps-env`, `apps-auth`, `apps-artisan`, `apps-run`, `apps-deploy-config` |
| `deploy`, `deploy audit` | `deploy-manage` |
| `yml` | `yml-view`, `yml-manage` |
| `ssl`, `www`, `aliases`, `redirect`, `proxies` | `ssl-manage`, `www-manage`, `aliases-*`, `redirects-*`, `proxies-*` |
| `db` | `dbs-view`, `dbs-create`, `dbs-manage` (anonymize: `apps-view` + `apps-env`) |
| `php`, `services`, `ssh-keys`, `smtp`, `health`, `ip-whitelist` | matching `*-view` / `*-manage` |
| `status`, `disk`, insights | `status-view`, `disk-view`, `*-view` |

Simplest: `cipi api token create --name=laptop --full-access`. Keep server and API current with `cipi self-update` so every command is available.


## PHP SDK

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/php-sdk

`cipi/sdk` is the **PHP client for the Cipi API**. From a Laravel app, a Symfony service or a plain script, one token calls the same surface as [cipi-cli](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client) and the [web panel](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui): apps, deploys, `cipi.yml`, domains, databases, backups and the server. It runs on your machine over HTTPS: no SSH, no shelling out to `cipi`.

```bash
$ composer require cipi/sdk
```

PHP 8.2+ with `ext-curl` and `ext-json`; Laravel optional. Source: [github.com/cipi-sh/sdk](https://github.com/cipi-sh/sdk) (MIT). The server needs [`cipi api`](https://cipi.sh/docs/api) and a token with only the abilities this code needs.

## Client 

```php
use Cipi\Sdk\Cipi;

$cipi = Cipi::connect(
    baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com',   // "/api" suffix optional
    token: getenv('CIPI_TOKEN') ?: '',
);

$apps = $cipi->apps()->list();
$job  = $cipi->deploys()->start('shop');  // 202 + job_id
$done = $cipi->wait($job);                // polls until completed or failed
```

Reads return the JSON body as an array; writes return a job you can `wait()` on. Plain `http://` is refused unless you pass `['allow_http' => true]` (for a local panel).

## Laravel 

Auto-discovered on Laravel 11, 12 and 13.

```bash
$ php artisan vendor:publish --tag=cipi-config
```

```bash
CIPI_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com
CIPI_TOKEN=
CIPI_TIMEOUT=30
```

```php
use Cipi\Sdk\Laravel\Facades\Cipi;

Cipi::apps()->list();
```

Or type-hint `Cipi\Sdk\Cipi`. The container holds one server; for another, call `Cipi::connect()` with its URL and token. Symfony and others register `Cipi::connect()` in their own container.

> [!tip] Install it next to [`cipi/agent`](https://cipi.sh/docs/mcp) and the app's MCP server gains panel tools: `panel_rollback`, `panel_deploy_audit`, `panel_db_backup`, `panel_job`, `panel_status`.

## Apps 

```php
$cipi->wait($cipi->apps()->create([
    'user'       => 'shop',
    'domain'     => 'shop.example.com',
    'repository' => 'git@github.com:acme/shop.git',
    'branch'     => 'main',
    'php'        => '8.6',
    'env'        => 'production',
    'node_build' => 'npm ci && npm run build',
]));

$cipi->apps()->update('shop', ['php' => '8.6']);
$cipi->apps()->suspend('shop');  $cipi->apps()->unsuspend('shop');
$cipi->apps()->recreateWebhook('shop', rotateSecret: true);
$cipi->wait($cipi->limits()->update('shop', ['fpm_max_children' => 10, 'disk_limit_gb' => 5]));

$cipi->basicAuth()->enable('shop', 'admin');
$cipi->wait($cipi->artisan()->run('shop', 'migrate --force'));
$cipi->wait($cipi->run()->execute('shop', 'composer install --no-dev'));
$cipi->logs()->get('shop', 'deploy');
```

Create accepts the fields of `POST /api/apps`: `user` and `domain` required, plus `repository`, `branch`, `php`, `env`, `custom`, `octane`, `engine`, `node_build`, or Node fields. Invalid values throw `ValidationException` (422).

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `env` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`, default `production`; picks `cipi-.yml` |
| `node_build` | Starts with `npm`, `npx`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, `bun` or `node`; `&&` and `;` allowed; no pipes, redirects or substitutions; max 200 characters |
| `limits()` | FPM children, `memory_limit`, Octane workers, queue workers, `disk_limit_gb` (soft, `null` removes it) |

After create (and edits that change repository or branch) the job result carries `repository_access`:

```php
$job = $cipi->wait($cipi->apps()->create($attributes));
$access = $job['data']['result']['repository_access'] ?? null;
if ($access && $access['status'] !== 'ok') {      // ok, nobranch or denied
    // $access['error'] is git's line, $access['hint'] the server command that fixes it
}
```

## Deploys, jobs and cipi.yml 

```php
$cipi->wait($cipi->deploys()->start('shop'));
$cipi->deploys()->rollback('shop');
$cipi->deploys()->unlock('shop');
$cipi->deploys()->audit('shop', days: 30);
$cipi->deploys()->status('shop', tail: 50);   // running, queued, interrupted, idle
$cipi->deploys()->history('shop', limit: 10);
$cipi->deploys()->last();                     // last run of every app
$cipi->deployConfig()->update('shop', ['keep_releases' => 5, 'migrate' => true]);

$cipi->jobs()->wait($job, timeoutSeconds: 120, intervalSeconds: 1.0);
```

`wait()` times out after 300 s by default and throws `JobFailedException` (payload on `$e->job`) when a job fails.

```php
$plan = $cipi->yml()->status('shop')['data'];      // file, env, valid, in_sync, changes, blockers
foreach ($plan['changes'] as $change) {
    echo $change['summary'], PHP_EOL;              // e.g. "PHP 8.5 → 8.6"
}
if ($plan['blockers'] === []) {
    $job = $cipi->jobs()->wait($cipi->yml()->apply('shop'), throwOnFailure: false);
    $outcome = $job['data']['result']['outcome'];  // applied, unchanged, partial, blocked, invalid, no-file
}
$cipi->yml()->enableAuto('shop');
```

> [!warning] With auto-apply on, anyone who can commit can change the app's aliases, PHP settings, limits, workers, deploy recipe, schedule, databases and backups. Ask for confirmation before enabling it for someone. Reads need `yml-view`, writes `yml-manage`.

## Domains and SSL 

```php
$cipi->aliases()->add('shop', 'www.shop.example.com');
$cipi->www()->forceToRoot('shop');
$cipi->redirects()->set('shop', 'https://example.com', 301, keepPath: true);
$cipi->redirects()->add('shop', '/blog/', 'https://blog.example.com', 301, true);
$cipi->proxies()->add('shop', prefix: '/api/', upstream: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000', stripPrefix: true);
$cipi->ssl()->install('shop');
$cipi->ssl()->install('shop', dns: 'cloudflare', account: 'prod', wildcard: true);
$cipi->ssl()->setDnsAccount($cloudflareToken, 'prod');   // sync, never returned
```

Redirects and proxies are tested with `nginx -t` and reverted on failure; the proxy loopback guard can't be bypassed. Node apps: `node()->status($app)`, `node()->restart($app)`.

## Env, databases and backups 

```php
$cipi->env()->update('shop', ['APP_ENV' => 'production'], ['TELESCOPE_ENABLED']);  // merge, unset
$cipi->authJson()->replace('shop', ['http-basic' => ['repo.example.com' => ['username' => 'token', 'password' => $secret]]]);

$cipi->wait($cipi->databases()->create('shop_reports', 'pgsql', app: 'shop'));
$cipi->databases()->backup('shop');
$cipi->databases()->password('shop');
$cipi->databases()->link('legacy', 'shop');
$cipi->wait($cipi->databases()->restoreLocal('shop', __DIR__.'/shop.sql.gz'));   // chunked upload
```

`restoreLocal()` streams the dump in chunks (not bound by `memory_limit`) and cancels the upload if anything is refused. The panel deletes uploads when the restore ends.

```php
$cipi->backups()->createProfile('nightly', [
    'scope' => 'all', 'every' => '1d', 'destinations' => ['s3'], 'keep_days' => 14, 'encrypt' => true,
]);
$cipi->backups()->status()['data']['uncovered'];   // what no enabled profile takes
$cipi->backups()->run('nightly');                  // starts and returns, not a job
$cipi->wait($cipi->backups()->verify('nightly'));
```

Destinations and their keys are configured on the server and never returned.

## Server 

```php
$cipi->server()->status();
$cipi->php()->install('8.6');
$cipi->ssh()->add($publicKey);
$cipi->services()->restart('php8.6-fpm');
$cipi->health()->update('shop', 'https://shop.example.com/up', 200);
$cipi->search()->enable('shop');
$cipi->disk()->usage();
$cipi->wait($cipi->node()->upgrade(24, restart: true));
$cipi->ipWhitelist()->replace(['203.0.113.10'], ensureClientIp: true);
$cipi->request('GET', '/apps/shop');               // any endpoint not wrapped yet
```

Packages, monitor, Zero Trust and disk usage are read-only, as on the API.

## Security 

| Protection | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Transport | HTTPS with verification; redirects never followed, so the token stays on your host |
| Token | Only in the `Authorization` header; whitespace or control characters rejected (no header injection); stripped from exceptions and `var_dump` |
| Retries | Reads may retry `429`/`503` with a short `Retry-After`; writes never |
| Limits | Responses over 16 MiB refused; 30 s timeout, 10 s connect |

```php
$cipi = Cipi::connect($url, $token, [
    'timeout' => 30, 'connect_timeout' => 10, 'max_retries' => 2,
    'max_response_bytes' => 16777216, 'allow_http' => false,
]);
```

One token per application, smallest ability set, kept in the environment, never committed. A missing ability is a 403, never a silent no-op.

## Errors 

| Status | Exception |
| --- | --- |
| 401 | `AuthenticationException` |
| 403 | `AuthorizationException` (missing ability, or IP allowlist) |
| 404 | `NotFoundException` |
| 409 | `ConflictException` |
| 422 | `ValidationException` (`errors()` with Laravel's bag) |
| 429 | `RateLimitException` (`retryAfter`) |
| 5xx | `ServerException` |
| none | `TransportException`, `ConfigurationException`; from `wait()`: `JobFailedException`, `TimeoutException` |

```php
try {
    $cipi->wait($cipi->deploys()->start('shop'));
} catch (JobFailedException $e) {
    $job = $e->job;
} catch (AuthorizationException $e) {
    // token lacks deploy-manage
}
```


## WHMCS module

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/whmcs

Sell Laravel and PHP hosting on your own servers. The official **WHMCS provisioning module** ([github.com/cipi-sh/whmcs](https://github.com/cipi-sh/whmcs), MIT) maps the WHMCS lifecycle to the [Cipi API](https://cipi.sh/docs/api): orders create apps, suspensions take them offline, terminations remove them. A self-contained drop-in, no Composer dependencies.

```flow
Order paid | WHMCS Create Account
POST /api/apps | isolated app on Cipi
Auto-SSL | Let's Encrypt (optional)
Lifecycle | suspend, change package, terminate
```

## Requirements 

WHMCS 8.x, a Cipi server with [`cipi api`](https://cipi.sh/docs/api), and a token with these abilities:

| Ability | For |
| --- | --- |
| `apps-view` | Test Connection, App Info |
| `apps-create` | Create Account |
| `apps-edit` | Change Package |
| `apps-suspend` | Suspend, Unsuspend |
| `apps-delete` | Terminate |
| `deploy-manage` | Deploy, Rollback, Unlock |
| `ssl-manage` | Install SSL, Auto-SSL |

## Install 

```tree
your-whmcs/
└── modules/servers/cipi/
    ├── cipi.php
    └── lib/CipiApiClient.php
```

1. Copy `modules/servers/cipi/` into your WHMCS root.
2. **System Settings → Servers → Add New Server**: type *Cipi (Laravel hosting)*, hostname = API base URL (no trailing slash), password = token, Secure = yes.
3. Create a hosting product on that server and set its module settings:

| Setting | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP Version | 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 8.6 | server default |
| App Type | `laravel` or `custom` | `laravel` |
| Git Repository (SSH) | Required for Laravel, optional for custom | — |
| Git Branch | Branch to deploy | `main` |
| Auto SSL | Certificate right after creation | No |

| App type | Cipi equivalent | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `laravel` | `cipi app create` | Laravel apps with Deployer releases, workers, database |
| `custom` | `cipi app create --custom` | WordPress, static sites, SPAs, any PHP; Git optional (SFTP-only hosting) |

## Lifecycle 

| WHMCS action | API call | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Test Connection | `GET /api/apps` | Token and reachability |
| Create Account | `POST /api/apps` | Provision, wait for the job, optional SSL |
| Suspend | `POST /api/apps/{name}/suspend` | 503 maintenance page, nothing deleted |
| Unsuspend | `POST /api/apps/{name}/unsuspend` | Normal vhost back |
| Change Package | `PUT /api/apps/{name}` | PHP, repository, branch |
| Terminate | `DELETE /api/apps/{name}` | Remove the app |

Admin buttons on the service page: **Install SSL**, **Deploy**, **Rollback Deploy**, **Unlock Deploy**, **App Info**. If Auto-SSL fails, the app is still created and a warning is logged. Every call is logged with `logModuleCall()` (Utilities → Logs → Module Log).

## Extend it 

The bundled `CipiApiClient` covers apps, deploys, SSL, aliases, databases and jobs, for your own hooks:

```php
require_once ROOTDIR . '/modules/servers/cipi/lib/CipiApiClient.php';
$client = new CipiApiClient('https://api.example.com', $token);
$client->addAlias('myapp', 'alias.example.com');
$client->createDatabase('myapp_extra');
$client->backupDatabase('myapp');
```

> [!note] The module adds no client-area tab. One-time secrets Cipi generates (SSH and database passwords, deploy key, webhook) aren't pushed to WHMCS: deliver them with a hook or your support workflow. For richer tooling use the [PHP SDK](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-sdk).


## Cipi vs alternatives

URL: https://cipi.sh/docs/vs-alternatives

Server tools fall into five families. Cipi sits in the first, but runs **on your own server, for free**, with a CLI, an optional panel, an API and MCP. This page tells you honestly where it fits and where something else is a better choice. Head-to-head pages: [all comparisons](https://cipi.sh/alternatives).

| Family | Examples | You pay | Who runs the control plane |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Server panels** for your VPS | **Cipi**, Laravel Forge, Ploi, RunCloud, Cleavr, Vito Deploy, CloudPanel | Cipi: nothing; SaaS panels: per server per month | Cipi and Vito: you; the rest: the vendor |
| **Managed PaaS** | Laravel Cloud, Ploi Cloud, Render, Sevalla, fortrabbit | Usage or resources | The vendor, on its cloud |
| **Self-hosted Docker PaaS** | Coolify, Dokku, Easypanel | Nothing | You, with containers |
| **Deploy tools** | Kamal | Nothing | You; provisioning is up to you |
| **Hosting panels** | cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin, HestiaCP, aaPanel | Licence (cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin) or nothing | You, built for shared hosting |

## What Cipi is 

> [!tip] **Free, MIT, on your VPS.** One installer turns Ubuntu into a hardened server; every app is an isolated cell with its own user, PHP pool, database and certificate. Zero-downtime Git deploys, versioned server settings in [`cipi.yml`](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml), backups, monitoring and security updates. Driven by a CLI, an optional [web panel](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui), a [REST API](https://cipi.sh/docs/api) and [MCP servers](https://cipi.sh/docs/mcp). Laravel-first, with [custom](https://cipi.sh/docs/custom-apps) and [Node](https://cipi.sh/docs/node-apps) apps for everything else.

## At a glance 

| | Cipi | Forge | Ploi | Vito Deploy | Coolify | Laravel Cloud |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cost of the tool | **Free** | from $12/server/mo | €8–30/server/mo | Free | Free | Usage-based |
| Runs on | Your VPS | Vendor SaaS | Vendor SaaS | Its own VPS | Your server | Vendor cloud |
| Root on the server | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Native Laravel stack (FPM, Octane) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Containers | Managed |
| Settings versioned in the repo | `cipi.yml` | No | No | No | Partly (compose) | Partly |
| Full CLI, scriptable | Yes | API + CLI | API | API | API | API + CLI |
| Web dashboard | Optional, self-hosted | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| MCP for AI assistants | Per app and per server | No | No | No | No | No |
| Config encrypted at rest | Vault (AES-256) | Not advertised | Not advertised | Not advertised | Not advertised | Managed |
| Your infrastructure data leaves the server | Never | Yes (US SaaS) | Yes (EU SaaS) | No | No | Yes |

Prices from each product's public pages; check them before deciding, they change.

## Server panels 

### Laravel Forge 

The benchmark: built by the Laravel team, polished and battle-tested at huge scale, with multi-cloud provisioning, teams and monitoring. **Choose Forge** if you want the most mature hosted dashboard and provider integrations. **Choose Cipi** to stop paying per server, keep management on the server itself (no SaaS to be reachable), version server settings in `cipi.yml`, script everything from the CLI and drive it from AI assistants. [Cipi vs Forge](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-laravel-forge).

### Ploi 

A Forge-like SaaS panel from the Netherlands, natively GDPR-friendly, with a clean UI and built-in backups and monitoring. **Choose Ploi** for a cheaper hosted GUI with EU data handling. **Choose Cipi** when you want no third party at all, no plan limits, and the CLI, API and MCP surface. Not to be confused with [Ploi Cloud](#vs-ploi-cloud). [Cipi vs Ploi](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-ploi).

### Vito Deploy 

The closest in spirit: free, open source, self-hosted, a GUI built with Laravel, teams and plugins. Vito runs as its own Laravel app with a database, usually on a dedicated VPS; Cipi lives on the server it manages and adds the panel only if you want it. Cipi adds `cipi.yml`, MCP, an encrypted vault, server sync, a deploy audit trail and automatic security patching. [Cipi vs Vito Deploy](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-vito-deploy).

### RunCloud, Cleavr, ServerPilot, moss.sh 

Hosted panels from roughly $8 to $49 per server per month. RunCloud and ServerPilot lean towards WordPress and generic PHP; Cleavr and moss.sh support Laravel through a hosted GUI (moss.sh caps deploys on its free tier). Cipi gives you Laravel-aware automation (Deployer releases, workers, scheduler, Horizon, Reverb, Octane) for nothing. [RunCloud](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-runcloud) · [Cleavr](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cleavr) · [ServerPilot](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-serverpilot) · [moss.sh](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-moss).

### CloudPanel
